data.description: A bidirectional, executable, visual specification environment for software systems, and its own first subject. The JSONC specification text is the single authority; the 3D scene, inspector, source editor and agent command line are views of, and editors for, one transactional semantic model.
data.name: Exegra
notes: Behavioral claims (invariant and temporal) are evaluated on the listed scenario traces only, never exhaustively, and the scenario state machines in this file are hand-maintained abstractions of the code: the correspondence between them and the code is not generated and not checked.

Structural claims are evaluated on the components and relationships declared here. The declared relationships are maintained by hand from the real imports and calls; the traceability check compares only module file paths with the disk, not imports.

Nothing of the runtime is generated from the model. No component is recorded as generated or partially generated. The generators in src/core/generate/ derive documents and reports (manifest, architecture document, claims report, task list), not code. Behaviour that is model-configured (parser structure checks, inspector controls, projections, node shapes and colours, and the entity kinds, properties and verification methods a specification declares in its vocabulary) is driven by data at runtime but written by hand.

Persistence exists only under the Vite development server (PERSISTENCE_AVAILABLE is import.meta.env.DEV). A production build is read-only: it bundles the shipped specs/*/spec.jsonc and layout.jsonc files, never saves, and reports the save state as read-only.

Presentation layout is stored per view in layout.jsonc as absolute [x, z] pins of leaf nodes rounded to 0.01. Position carries no meaning, but a pin is not relative to anything, so a changed layout engine or a changed model leaves old pins where they were.

DISCREPANCY (claim edits-only-via-transactions is violated): the toolbar's Import sends a whole project bundle through the persistence client, development-server plugin and workspace service, which overwrite spec.jsonc, layout.jsonc and results.json directly. That path does not pass the transaction system: the toolbar only analyzes the bundle's spec.jsonc with analyzeSpec before sending it (it refuses a bundle with syntax errors and merely notes validation errors), there is no validation gate and no base-hash conflict check at the write, and the project of that name is replaced wholesale. The session then reopens the project and loads whatever was written, including a specification with validation errors, which then rejects edits until they are fixed. Every other editing surface reaches the specification file only through the transaction system (claim editing-surfaces-except-import-via-transactions).

Adopting a change made outside the process (Project.reload, used by the session's file watcher and its conflict resolution) accepts any text that parses, including a specification with validation errors, and refuses only syntax errors. It clears the undo and redo history and is not itself undoable, because undo would write older text over the newer file on disk. The session also refuses to switch projects while a save is pending, in conflict or in error.

The shipped projects are specs/exegra (this file), specs/benchmark (generated by tools/make-benchmark.js). Any other directory under specs/ is a linked project: local data that is ignored by git, with a project.jsonc naming a specification kept in another repository (tools/import-markdown.js can generate one from a Markdown specification). The multiplayer platform specification is not shipped: it is a test fixture at tests/fixtures/multiplayer/spec.jsonc used only by tests.

A specification can declare its own entity kinds, properties of any kind (including reference-typed and list-typed ones) and verification methods through its vocabulary. A claim whose method is a declared verification method is carried out outside Exegra: it is reported with evaluator external:<method> and a status that comes only from evidence, never from an evaluation by Exegra. The claim kind requirement exists in the meta-model.

The layout of a scene is chosen per view: the viewer's preference (kept in browser storage, not in the specification or the layout file), else the view's display.layout, else automatic. Automatic layout computes four methods and scores them; the scoring weights are hand-chosen constants and the choice depends on the viewport's shape, so the same view can be arranged differently in a differently shaped window. Pins in layout.jsonc apply under every method.

Recorded verification results (evidence/results.json) are keyed by evidence id and carry an outcome and a timestamp. They are not tied to the model hash or to the code revision, so a stale result is not detected as stale.

Applied edits are saved last-write-wins at the text level: the session writes the current text when it flushes, so several quick commits may be saved as one write. The edit-flow machines in this file model one write per commit.
No schema migration exists. A specification whose "exegra" version differs from 0.1 is rejected with an error whose text mentions an `exegra migrate` command that does not exist.

The browser tests (tests/browser/exegra.spec.js, interaction.spec.js and mobile.spec.js; a local-*.spec.js file tests a linked project and is not tracked) are separate from `npm test`; they run only through `npm run test:browser` or `exegra verify` without --skip-browser. Evidence of kind test shows no recorded execution until `exegra verify` has recorded results.

The evidence reference syntax `<path>#<title pattern>` accepted by `exegra verify` allows only letters, digits, underscore, dot, slash, hyphen, space, hash and colon. `exegra validate` reports any test reference outside that syntax as `evidence.ref-unsafe` (src/core/evidence-ref.js, shared with verify), so a test title containing a comma or semicolon is referenced by a prefix of its title.
The `projects` relationship kind is declared with dependency false in this file: a projection does not require its renderer, so a dependency graph does not follow it.

implementation.notes: types.js holds JSDoc typedefs only. The directory src/core also contains projections.js, layout.js with the modules under layout/, and generate/, which this file classifies under visualization and tooling by responsibility, and own.js, claimed by queries; they import nothing outside src/core.

responsibilities: Derive the model from specification text and validate it
Apply typed operations atomically as source-preserving text edits
Evaluate claims and simulate state machines on the model

implementation.notes: Grouping only; the code lives in the child components.

implementation.notes: Hand-written data file.

data.name: Meta-model
data.purpose: Describes entity kinds, their properties, the built-in categories and relationship kinds and the top-level sections of a specification as data.
responsibilities: Define which properties each entity kind accepts and their types
Define the built-in vocabulary (categories, relationship kinds, shapes, colours, projections) that a specification may extend
Define the id pattern and the schema version (0.1)

Define the claim kinds (structural, invariant, temporal, measured, requirement) and the view definition: filter (categories, relationship kinds, within, tags, entity kinds) and display (ports, colour by, reference depth, layout method)
Define the record and copy kinds of the data model: field types, personal-data classes, roles, copy scopes (shared, per-session, per-principal, internal) and the units of freshness and erasure bounds
unknowns: The built-in entity kinds, claim kinds, claim evaluation methods and projections are fixed per build. A specification can add entity kinds, properties of any kind, categories, relationship kinds and verification methods (carried out outside Exegra) through its vocabulary, but it cannot add an evaluation method that Exegra itself runs.

implementation.notes: Hand-written data module used by the parser, validator, evaluator and inspector.

data.name: Claim method registry
data.purpose: Declares the supported claim evaluation methods with their parameters, and the five claim statuses.
responsibilities: List each method, the claim kinds it can evaluate and its typed parameters
Define the claim status labels and tones that every consumer shows
Declare `negatives` as a parameter of every trace method (state-invariant, precedes, eventually, never): a list of {scenario, faults}, each one of the claim's scenarios run with extra faults
Declare the refines method: one implementation behavior and optionally the scenarios whose traces are checked
unknowns: The registry declares methods but the evaluator implements them separately; adding an entry without code leaves the claim not evaluated.

implementation.notes: Outside the verdict path: it only parses text and maps locations; the model is derived by model-derivation in Lean.

data.name: Parser
data.purpose: The text layer of the specification: parses the JSONC source (comments, trailing commas, syntax errors with locations), hands the document to the model derivation in the Lean kernel and maps the raw paths it reports to lines and columns.
responsibilities: Parse JSONC with comments and trailing commas, reporting syntax errors with locations
Encode the document for the kernel with every object's members in source order and repeated keys kept, and pass the meta-model and the claim method registry as data
Map every raw path and part the kernel reports (node, key of a member, first character) to an offset, length, line and column, and put the line of the earlier declaration into an id.duplicate message

Rebuild the model the rest of the shell reads (entities by id and kind, references, expressions, effective meta-model, vocabulary, semantic hash) from the kernel's reply, with prototype-free data objects as jsonc-parser builds them
unknowns: The whole text is re-parsed on every commit and on every source-editor analysis; there is no incremental parsing. Measured 2026-11-18 in Node 24 on Windows 10 (wasm64, median of 10 warm runs, parse and hash): specs/exegra (788 KB) 243 ms through the Lean kernel against 35 ms for the JavaScript it replaced; specs/benchmark (134 KB) 67 ms against 9 ms. Of the 243 ms about 95 ms is Exegra.Json.parse reading the request (WG-4797), 27 ms the derivation, 10 ms reference resolution, 33 ms the hash and 45 ms writing the reply. In Chromium (Playwright, tests/browser/lean-core.spec.js) the same parse and hash take 312 ms (median of 7).
The schema.version error message tells the user to run an `exegra migrate` command that does not exist.

implementation.notes: The rules are hard-coded. Claim parameter checks read the claim method registry, the gap rules read `expected` flags of the effective meta-model and view filters are checked against the effective vocabulary.

data.name: Validator
data.purpose: Applies whole-model semantic rules to a parsed model and reports errors, warnings and specification gaps; analyzeSpec composes parser and validator.
responsibilities: Check containment, behaviors, transitions, effects, faults, scenarios, claim parameters and views
Accept an evaluation method the specification declares as a verification method (it takes no parameters), and report any other method this build does not run as unsupported
Check every expression's references against the scope it is used in

Report gaps (missing purpose, unconnected component, unused event, claim that can only rest on external evidence and has none) as info diagnostics; a requirement claim is not reported for lacking evidence
Provide analyzeSpec: parse, then validate only when the structure is sound

Check events that name a contract: a role is required, the payload fields are among the inputs (request) or outputs (response), every input that is not optional is present, an error carries a code among the contract's errors, and declared field types are assignable to the contract's; an unknown contract is a reference error

Run the data model's consistency checks (record keys and copy fields name declared fields, bounds have units) as errors and its six data rules as warnings, each naming the record or copy and the field
Check each negative of a trace claim: its scenario is one of the claim's scenarios, and its faults are a non-empty list of declared faults none of which that scenario already activates
Report integrity rules: an invalid rule as an error, a vacuous rule as a warning, and each violation with the rule severity (integrity.violated), left out of analyzeSpec's blocking error count

Check refinement declarations: only an implementation-level behavior refines, the refined behavior does not refine in turn, refines comes with a refinement mapping, the mapping names only states and transitions of the right sides and variables of the model, its expressions read only the implementation's variables, and every implementation state and transition and every model variable is mapped; a refines claim names one refining behavior and only scenarios that run it

Check timer delays read at run time ({expr, simulate}): only on an implementation-level machine, expr an expression of a number over the machine variables, time and the event payload, and simulate the delay a simulated run uses (simulationInputV2 lowers the timer with it)

Check time and integers in implementation-level machines (src/core/readiness-time.js, WG-4902): a variable compared with time holds a value set from time wherever it is read (ready.time-epoch); time - x is read only after x <= time (ready.time-difference); the scenarios running the machine agree on a time unit, fixed delays are whole milliseconds and a machine reading time runs in ms (ready.delay-unit); literals, integer initial values and scenario payload values are within their integer range, at most 2^53 - 1 (ready.number-bound)

Check the realisation and durability of machines (src/core/realisation.js, WG-4922): behavior.realisation and contract.deployment (shipped or target, defaulting from the component's implementation status; an explicit shipped on a not-implemented component is behavior.realisation-subject or contract.deployment-subject) and storage.durability (record or memory; a memory machine names no record, creates none and declares no transaction, or storage.durability)

Check residency (src/core/residency.js): follow each record a tenant class binds to its owner, the holder of each copy and both ends of each relationship that carries it, and report a component that cannot keep a tenant of the class in its permitted regions (residency.record-outside, residency.copy-outside, residency.flow-outside) unless an active residency exception names that copy or flow; a holder of bound data states its placement (residency.placement-missing) and a per-region one has an instance in every provisioned region (residency.region-uncovered); placement and regions agree (component.placement-regions); a tenant class has one selector and at least one region (tenant-class.selector, tenant-class.provisioned-in); an exception names one copy or flow of bound data, its durations are durations, a bounded one states its purge and a renewal window is shorter than its longest duration (residency.exception-target, residency.exception-duration, residency.exception-purge, residency.exception-renewal)

Check quota pools (src/core/pools.js): at least one pooled limit with a unique lower-case name (pool.limits), exactly one of quota and a positive perMember (pool.limit-contribution), a pooled quota counted per tenant over the pool's window as a rate (pool.quota-scope, pool.quota-window, pool.limit-kind) and held by the pool's component (pool.held-by), usage and exemption events with the payload fields the pool reads (pool.usage-event, pool.event-payload), the window, over-share count and release (pool.window, pool.over-share, pool.release), 1 to 4 modelled members (pool.model-members), an exemption role that confers its capability (pool.exemption-capability) and machine ids no entity takes (pool.machine-id); a scenario runs a behavior or a pool (scenario.empty), and a claim expression reads only variables of the machines of pools every listed scenario runs (expr.reference)
unknowns: A residency exception's expiry, continuous renewal and purge are recorded and shape-checked but not executed, so claims about them are not decided by exploration (WG-5282).

implementation.notes: The validator and the claim evaluator use src/core/expr.js. The simulation engine has its own implementation of the same language in Rust (engine/exegra-engine/src/expr.rs), held to the same parse and evaluation semantics and error messages by the conformance goldens.

data.name: Expression language
data.purpose: A small side-effect-free expression language for guards, effect values and claim expressions; no host-language evaluation is involved.
responsibilities: Tokenize and parse expressions (implication, boolean and arithmetic operators, comparisons, string and number literals, dotted references with hyphenated ids)
Evaluate an expression against a caller-supplied reference resolver
List the references an expression uses so the validator can check scope

Evaluate with the declared types of references when the caller gives them (WG-4902): checked integer arithmetic in u8, u16, u32, i32 and in u64 and i64 limited to +-(2^53 - 1), integer division truncating toward zero and remainder with the sign of the dividend, an absent option read as null; structural equality of lists and objects always; the same rules as eval in formal/Exegra/Expr.lean and the generated code (docs/semantics.md, Values, numbers and time)

implementation.notes: The Lean kernel of the hash only. The JavaScript that calls it is hash-binding (src/core/hash.js), a separate component, so this component's dependencies are only the Lean definitions it uses. Stable JSON output and SHA-256 are stable-serialization.

data.name: Normal form and hash
data.purpose: Produces the deterministic normal form of a model (independent of comments, whitespace, key order, top-level declaration order and source positions) and its 53-bit semantic hash, in the verified kernel.
responsibilities: Normal form: schema version, vocabulary and the top-level declarations sorted by id with every object's keys sorted as JavaScript sorts strings (UTF-16 code units)

Semantic hash: cyrb53 over the UTF-16 code units of the normal form's JSON text, bit-identical to the JavaScript it replaced; used for revision identity, optimistic concurrency of transactions and claim results

Prove that the hash depends only on semantic content: declaration order and presentation (Exegra.Model.Model.semanticHash_presentation) and key order at every depth (Exegra.Hash.semanticHash_key_order); what runs is the definition (Exegra.Hash.semanticHash'_eq)
unknowns: The hash is not cryptographic (cyrb53); it identifies revisions and detects change, it does not resist collisions.
The key-order theorem assumes distinct keys in every object; the derivation produces such values (it assigns members like JavaScript), but that is not itself stated as a theorem yet.

implementation.notes: own.js is a one-function helper; it is claimed here because the lookup it provides is imported by the other core modules that read spec-supplied keys.

data.name: Model queries
data.purpose: Answers containment, dependency, selection, reference and contract questions about a model for every consumer.
responsibilities: Resolve ports to components, list children, ancestors, descendants and owned entities
Build the directed component graph and traverse dependencies
Select components by id, category, kind, tag, trust zone or containment
Find the declaration site of an entity kind
Provide own(), the own-property lookup that the parser, validator, claim evaluator, queries and Project use for every spec-supplied key

implementation.notes: The operation table is hand-written; CreateEntity looks up declaration sites in the meta-model. Tx keeps the index of declarations, the windows over edited declarations and the pending appends; Project.apply's perOperation option runs the reference path that re-derives after every edit.

data.name: Transaction system
data.purpose: Applies typed operations atomically as source-preserving text edits, with revisions, undo, redo, reload and commit notification; it is the only place where a project's state changes.
responsibilities: Check operation preconditions and compute JSONC edits that keep comments and formatting
Reject any transaction whose resulting specification has validation errors (violations of integrity rules excepted) or whose layout would be unreadable; nothing changes on rejection
Keep presentation edits (layout) out of the specification text
Record history sufficient for undo and redo and increment a revision on every commit

Adopt text that changed outside the process (reload): text with syntax errors is refused, any text that parses is adopted, including text with validation errors; the adoption clears the undo and redo stacks and is itself not undoable
Leave the model and its semantic hash as they were when a commit changes only presentation text
Notify subscribers synchronously after each commit

Reject a transaction that adds a violation of an integrity rule of severity error that the project did not have before (the ratchet), with the counterexamples; existing violations do not block unrelated edits

Re-derive the model once per transaction, not once per operation: keep an index of where every entity is declared that follows creations, property edits, removals, replacements of nested declarations and id changes, re-derive only for an operation that reads references, expressions or entity data (deletion, rename, source replacement) or after an edit the index cannot follow, and splice the edits of each declaration's lines into the text once; the resulting text, failures and verdict are those of re-deriving after every edit, and a transaction whose index is found not to match its model is replayed that way
unknowns: History, undo and redo stacks are unbounded in memory and are not persisted: undo is lost on reload and per CLI invocation.

Only operation transactions and replacement sources are validated before they commit. Undo and redo restore text that was committed before and do not validate again, and reload commits any text that parses, so the model after a reload can carry validation errors.
The session never passes expectRevision or expectHash; only the CLI uses the optimistic checks (--expect-hash).

A deletion or a rename re-derives the model of the current text before it plans its edits, because references and expressions of entities edited earlier in the transaction are known only to a derivation: about 2.6 s each on a 7 MB specification (WG-4980).

The validation of a transaction's result is a full validation: rule and example results are not cached per entity (WG-4974). Measured on a 7 MB specification, validation is about 0.9 s of a single-property apply; the model derivation is about 2.6 s.

data.description: Submit one operation or an array of operations as one transaction.
data.name: Apply transaction
Claim evaluator
data.purpose: Evaluates claims against a model and recorded evidence results, reporting a status, scope and counterexample that never overstate what was checked.
responsibilities: Evaluate structural claims (no-relationship, reachable, only-via, has-port, property-defined, acyclic) on the component graph; report a selector that selects nothing as inconclusive, never verified; reachable needs a path of at least one relationship (a target that is also a source does not count); only-via is inconclusive when no directed path of the kinds leads from any source to any target at all, and when every source is itself a via component (both hold by construction, not by the model)

Evaluate invariant and temporal claims on traces of the listed scenarios (state-invariant, precedes, eventually, never), stating that only those traces were checked; never report a vacuous trace check as verified: an implication whose antecedent is never true, a never whose event cannot occur, a precedes whose then-event never happens and traces with zero steps are inconclusive; an eventually whose occurrence is only the scenario's own scripted input is inconclusive, because the input is not a reaction of the system
Derive the status of external-evidence claims only from evidence entities and recorded execution results

Compare recorded facts with the current stamps the caller passes (tools/tree-stamp.js): an evidence result or external tool outcome whose stamp is not the records stamp of the tree, and a Lean theorem check whose formal hash is not that of the current formal/ sources, is stale; a stale positive fact never makes a claim positive (not-evaluated, an explanation starting with Stale, freshness stale and the diagnostic claim.stale-evidence or claim.stale-theorem) and a stale contradicting fact still counts; without current stamps a result resting on recorded facts carries freshness unverifiable and the diagnostic claim.freshness-unverifiable
Refuse a lean-theorem claim that names no implementation constant in about, or whose about constant is opaque or reported implemented_by, extern or partial
Report a claim whose method is a verification method declared by the specification with evaluator external:<method>: Exegra runs nothing and the status comes only from evidence
Check a trace step by step for the simulator panel (checkTrace)
Add the automatic contract-conformance checks of a trace to the checks of checkTrace (src/core/contract-trace.js), as failed checks with the step

Evaluate data-model claims (method data-model, a list of rules) on the records and copies of the model: violated with the first finding as counterexample, verified when every listed rule had something to check and found nothing, inconclusive when a listed rule had nothing to check

Run every declared negative of a trace claim (its scenario with the scenario's own faults plus the negative's) and report the claim verified only when it holds on its scenarios and each negative, at least one, violates it; a trace claim with no negative, or with a negative that does not definitely violate it, is inconclusive and the explanation says which

Evaluate refines claims (src/core/refinement.js): in the trace of each scenario that runs the implementation behavior, check that its initial configurations and every transition it fires map through its refinement mapping to the transition its model would fire (from, to, event, guard true and first in declaration order, effects giving the mapped post-variables, the same emitted events) or to a stutter that changes no mapped state or variable and emits nothing; violated at the first failing step with the steps up to it as a trace and a reason; inconclusive when a run ends in an error, a model expression reads what the mapping does not define, or no step matched a model transition

In refines claims, tell a transition's queued entries apart into emits and timers by its effects, compare timers only with a model transition that sets timers, and read other behaviors named by model expressions from the same trace configuration, through the machine that refines them when they do not run themselves
unknowns: Behavioral results hold for the listed scenario traces only; there is no exhaustive state-space exploration and no probabilistic evaluation.

Claim evaluation runs on the caller's thread. In the application session.evaluate runs it on the main thread inside every semantic commit, and trace and metric claims run engine scenarios there (src/core/claims.js), unlike the Simulation tab, which runs its scenario in the engine worker. The cost on large models is not measured (WG-4775, finding F06).

Refines claims are checked on the deterministic trace of each scenario with its own faults, not over every delivery order and fault subset the explorer enumerates: the explorer returns state-invariant verdicts, not steps (WG-4852).

Freshness is reported through not-evaluated, the freshness field and diagnostics, not as a status component of its own; the status lattice with freshness as a part (milestone M3 of docs/foundations.md) replaces these rules. The tree stamp is coarse: any edit of a stamped file makes every evidence result stale until verify runs again, not only the results that depend on it.

A lean-theorem claim is not bound to what its statement says: a theorem that mentions the named code but states nothing about it (a tautology over it) is still proved, and the recorded statement hash is not compared with anything (statement binding: milestone M3; admission of statement changes: milestone M10 of docs/foundations.md).

data.description: Evaluate every claim or one claim of a model.
data.name: Evaluate claims

implementation.notes: engine/ holds the library and native binary (exegra-engine) and the WebAssembly crate (exegra-engine-wasm). npm run build:engine (tools/build-engine.js) compiles the WebAssembly crate and binds it with wasm-bindgen into src/engine/pkg/, which is generated, not committed, and left out of the traceability surface. src/core/engine.js is the only module that loads an engine, and it loads the Lean core through the call boundary (src/core/lean.js); the Rust engine in src/engine/pkg/ is loaded only by tools/rust-engine.js, the differential oracle. src/app/engine-runner.js and src/app/engine-worker.js run the Simulation tab's runs off the main thread.

data.name: Simulation engine
data.purpose: Executes the state machines of a scenario as a deterministic discrete-event simulation over logical time.
responsibilities: Order events by logical time and scheduling sequence, deliver each to every behavior of the scenario
Fire at most one transition per behavior and event, evaluating guards against the configuration at the start of the step
Apply faults (drop, delay, enable or disable a transition, inject an event; in format 2 also duplicate, lose and retry an event as the generated runtime would) and record them in the trace
End a run as quiescent, step-limit (default 1000) or error

Run as one engine everywhere: the Lean core (formal/), called as engine.run through the Lean call boundary and loaded only through src/core/engine.js in the browser and in Node (the Simulation tab runs it in a Web Worker so a long run never blocks the page), and as the native binary exegra-lean compiled from the same C
unknowns: Format 2 (integer time units, instances, routes, resources and resource faults, workloads, links, timers, request classes and seeded randomness) runs in the Lean engine (formal/Exegra/Format2.lean, Api/Engine.lean); the Rust engine implements the same format as the differential oracle. crash-instance, meters and the cost metric are not built yet (planned: WG-4741).

One configuration copy per step dominates the cost of large format-2 runs (about 10 to 40 us per step); the queueing fixtures (about 7 and 15 minutes) are gated by EXEGRA_FIXTURES=1 (planned: WG-4741).
Behaviors are flat: a component cannot yet be simulated at a chosen depth, as its abstract behavior or as its children (planned: WG-4666).

data.description: Run a scenario to completion (runScenario, runEngine), or step through a finished trace (createTraceCursor, createSimulation).
data.name: Run scenario

implementation.notes: Views are declared in the specification and shapes, colours and line styles come from the model's vocabulary; the projection code is hand-written.

data.name: Projection system
data.purpose: Derives a flat scene (nodes, edges, legend, notes) from the model for a declared view with one of six projections (structural, claims, behavior, references, data, reader); a view is never a separate dataset and every node and edge is backed by a real entity.
responsibilities: List the views declared in the specification, plus an implicit view for each projection type without a declared view
Project the structural, claims and behavior projections, applying view filters (categories, relationship kinds, within, tags) and display options

Project references: the focused entity (the session's selection) and every entity within display.depth reference hops (1 to 3, in either direction, any entity kind, declared kinds included), at most 150 nodes with a note naming what was left out; filter.entityKinds restricts the kinds drawn, and without a focus it draws every entity of those kinds when there are at most 300, otherwise only a note asking for a selection
Handle collapsed subsystems (lifted edges), hidden entities, isolation, claim focus, scenario focus and the current simulation step
Take node shapes, colours and line styles from the effective vocabulary of the model; entities of declared kinds take the shape and colour their kind declares

Derive the message flow of a simulation step (src/core/flows.js): the sender is the subject of the behavior whose transition emitted the event, or outside for a scenario stimulus or an injected fault; the receivers are the subjects of the behaviors that fired on it; the path follows the scene edge between their drawn nodes, and is marked unshown when only a relationship the view does not draw connects them, or undeclared when none does

Project the Data view when the model declares records or copies: records, copies and the components that own or hold them, with edges from of, heldBy and owner; copies with data-rule findings are marked violated
Register the reader projection, which draws no scene: its views are read on the reader surface
unknowns: The cost of projection on large models has no recorded measurement; the benchmark specification exists for that purpose but no result is recorded.
The references projection draws nothing but a note until an entity is selected, unless the view filters to entity kinds.

data.description: Project a model and a view into a SceneModel.
data.name: Project scene

implementation.notes: layout.js is the entry (layoutScene, chooseLayout, LAYOUT_METHODS, scorePlacement); the other modules hold the shared recursion (solve.js, model.js), the four arrangers, the score and the shared sizes.

data.name: Layout engine
data.purpose: Computes deterministic layouts of a scene on the ground plane by one of four methods, recursively over containers, honouring pinned leaf positions, and can choose the method by scoring the results.
responsibilities: Offer the methods layered (dependency layers left to right), layered-down (front to back), packed (no flow direction, connected siblings in tight rows) and radial (best-connected node at the centre, rings around it); each arranges the siblings of one container level and the shared recursion encloses them in their container with padding
Place pinned leaf nodes at their absolute [x, z] pin and keep their container enclosing them
Tolerate cycles, self edges and edges across containers
Shape the result towards a target width-to-depth ratio supplied by the caller (default 1.6)

chooseLayout (method auto): compute every method, score each placement (aspect against the target, mean edge length, edge crossings, whitespace area, fixed weights) and return the lowest score, ties going to the earlier method, together with every score
unknowns: Pins are absolute positions; nothing re-anchors them when the model changes.
The score weights are fixed constants chosen by hand; no recorded measurement shows that the lowest score is the most readable layout. Crossings are counted on at most 400 sampled edges.
Automatic layout computes all four methods on every recompute; its cost on large scenes has no recorded measurement.

data.name: Three.js scene renderer
data.purpose: Draws a SceneModel and its placement in 3D with Three.js, as a function of (scene, placement, selection, highlight, camera) with no domain state of its own.
responsibilities: Diff the scene incrementally by node and edge id and animate placement changes

Draw node shapes, container slabs, edge curves with line styles, status colours and CSS2D labels with clutter management; the label layer is its own stacking context, so a label (even a message in flight, lifted above the other labels) never covers the interface around the scene
Run a requestAnimationFrame loop that renders only when something changed, and report frame statistics

Detect picking, hover, double click, dragging of leaf nodes and connect-mode clicks and report them through callbacks; it never edits the model. Touch: a tap allows 10 px of movement, a second finger makes the gesture a pinch or pan with no tap, and a node is dragged only after the finger has rested on it for 350 ms (a swipe that starts on a node orbits the camera)

Animate a simulation step's message: a marker labelled with the event travels from the sender's node along the drawn edge to each receiver (backwards along it for a reply), drops in from above for a request from outside, travels straight for a relationship the view does not draw, and travels straight in the violation colour when no relationship is declared; only the current step's message is in flight, so stepping quickly or playing never piles markers up; a message's clock advances by at most a twenty-fourth of its travel time per drawn frame, so where frames are slow (software rendering of a large scene) it travels more slowly and stays readable instead of vanishing after a few frames
unknowns: No frame-rate or load-time measurement is recorded for the 396-component benchmark specification.

Pointer, drag and connect handling live inside src/render/scene-view.js, which this file assigns to the renderer; the split between rendering and interaction is not a module boundary (see visual-interaction).

Route renderer callbacks to the session: select and hover, activate (collapse a subsystem or fit), move (MovePresentationNode operations) and connect (open the connect dialog)

Run the verification pipeline: validation, traceability, execution of test evidence and recording of the results, each with the records stamp of the tree; record a reference that skipped, wholly or in part, as not-run instead of keeping an older pass

Fail verify when, against the claim statuses and counterexample fingerprints the last passing run recorded (claimBaseline), a positive claim falls to a lower status (inconclusive and not-evaluated included) or is removed, or an expected-violated claim's counterexample changes, unless --accept-change names the claim; a failing run keeps the earlier baseline

Copy a project's specification into its SQLite store and write it back as text (store import, store export), refusing an export over a specification that changed since the store last synchronised with it

Register a specification file and product files as a project from a script (project add, remove, list: specs/<name>/project.jsonc with paths relative to the project directory, refusing an existing project without --force and a name that is not a project name), and take the project inline (--spec, --product) on the read-only commands, so a job needs no registration

Acknowledge admit reasons by code (admit --accept, repeatable or comma separated): a reason that carries acknowledgeable true and whose code is accepted no longer blocks admission and is listed under acknowledged; a reason without it (a failure rather than a decision) cannot be accepted, and passing its code is the error admit.not-acknowledgeable

Report in admit what a change does to privileges and guarantees as acknowledgeable reasons: admit.privilege-change for every capability added to a role, grant, delegation or token scope and every new or changed grant or delegation without maxDuration (capabilities removed are listed under diff.privilege.removed, not as a reason), and admit.guarantee-weakened for a copy class whose freshness or erasure bound is looser than another class of the same record, a changed or removed retention, integrity rule or claim (before and after)

Report a new claim that is realised by code and cannot be decided at specification time (a requirement, a claim of an external verification method or of external-evidence) that names a milestone and has no result yet as pendingRealisation instead of a weak claim; a requirement without a milestone is the reason admit.requirement-without-milestone

Admit a change set (admit): evaluate the specification before and after the operations are applied in memory through Project.apply, report the diff of claim statuses, validation diagnostics, readiness gaps and integrity violations, and admit it only when no claim got worse (a fall from a positive status to not-evaluated included), no claim that was positive is removed unless admit.claim-removed is accepted, no validation error or integrity violation is new and every claim it creates is verified or proved; report the check and grounding of every claim (counts before and after, and each claim it creates) and reject a claim the change creates that is holds-by-construction or restated-scenario (admit.claim-vacuous), single-trace (admit.claim-single-trace) or self-contained (admit.claim-self-contained), each reason marked acknowledgeable; write the specification, as apply does, only with --write and an admitted verdict
Show the check and grounding of each claim (src/core/claim-strength.js) in the results of claims and evaluate

Writing the spec file and the layout file are two separate writes; if the second conflicts, the first has already been written.
No MCP server or other protocol wrapper exists; the command line is the only agent-facing interface.

Admit and verify compare claim statuses, not what the claims say: an edit of a claim's statement or evaluate is reported (admit.guarantee-weakened) but not ranked, and the verify baseline starts with the first passing run that records it (milestone M10 of docs/foundations.md).

Under the workflow's concurrency group a queued run is replaced when a newer push arrives, so an intermediate push may never be deployed; a disabled workflow, Pages not set to GitHub Actions or a push marked to skip CI publish nothing.

The GitHub Pages site is the production build: read-only, it shows the specifications as of the last push to main with the evidence results recorded in specs/exegra/evidence/results.json, and, the Lean core being wasm64, it does not run in stable Safari.
The production build contains no persistence service: it bundles the shipped specs and is read-only.

responsibilities: Report declared modules missing on disk and files under src, cli and tools (.js, .json, .css, .html) plus index.html and vite.config.js that no component claims, leaving out generated build output (src/engine/pkg/) and files whose name starts with local- (local data, ignored by git)

Through `verify`: validate, check traceability, execute each evidence of kind test with node --test or Playwright and record outcomes and the traceability result in results.json, then re-evaluate claims with them
Refuse an evidence reference with characters outside letters, digits, underscore, dot, slash, hyphen, space, hash and colon, and time a test run out after ten minutes

Reuse the outcomes that `npm test` and `npm run test:browser` already recorded (reporters in tools/ writing .outcomes/, each stamped with a hash over the tracked files, the untracked files git does not ignore and the generated engine builds) instead of running the same test again: an evidence reference is answered from the recorded run only when the run was complete, the tree did not change during it and its stamp equals the stamp of the tree verify runs on; a reference that matches no recorded test, a failure, or a skipped browser test is run as before, and a unit test that skipped itself is recorded as skipped. results.json says for each outcome whether it was run or reused; `verify --fresh` reuses nothing

Decide what a reference's matched tests establish with one function on the fresh path (node's TAP output, Playwright's summary) and the reuse path (the recorded outcomes) alike: only leaf tests count, a describe block is not a test, todo tests are recorded as todo, and a reference passes only when at least one matched test executed and passed and none failed, skipped or is a todo

Stamp what it records: the records stamp (the tree stamp without specs/<project>/evidence/results.json and specs/<project>/generated/) on every evidence result, and on every Lean theorem check the hash of the formal/ sources checked, the records stamp and the sha256 of the theorem statement as Lean printed it
unknowns: Only evidence of kind test is executed; measurement, document and review evidence stay author-entered.

The traceability check compares paths only: it does not check that a module implements what its component claims, nor that relationships match imports. Its surface is src/, cli/ and tools/ with the extensions .js, .json, .css and .html, plus index.html and vite.config.js: a .mjs file is outside it (tools/bench-mm1.mjs was unclaimed until this correction), and formal/ and engine/ are outside it too, so an unclaimed Lean or Rust file is not reported.
Browser tests need Chrome and the Vite development server; `verify --skip-browser` skips them and records their evidence as not run, unless its earlier result was recorded on the same tree stamp.

A whole-file evidence reference to a test file with a test that skips itself where a tool is missing (Lean, a native binary) is not a pass in such an environment; the reference passes only where every matched test runs.

The Lean checker does not yet report implemented_by, extern or partial for a definition (tools/lean-theorems.js reports kind, axioms, the kernel check, the constants in the statement and the statement text), so only opaque constants are refused for that reason today.

data.name: Markdown importer
data.purpose: A command line tool that converts a Markdown specification, structured Markdown kept in another repository, into the specification file of a linked project, a specification that declares its own entity kinds and verification methods.
responsibilities: Read the Markdown (white paper, roadmap, the specification documents and the verification document) and the git commit of that repository, plus the project's import map (specs/<project>/import-map.jsonc), which supplies what Exegra requires and the Markdown does not state (the project's name and title, where those documents are, and a category per component); fail with a message naming a component that has no entry in the map

Work one way and deterministically: the same input gives the same bytes, it never writes to the Markdown repository and it states nothing the Markdown does not; the Markdown stays the authority and the generated file says it must not be edited by hand
Record what it recognised but could not map: each kind of loss with a count and examples is printed and also written into the generated specification's system notes
With --check, compare the generated text with the file on disk and exit 1 when it is out of date; usage errors exit 2

It writes the project's specification file directly with node:fs, not through the workspace service or the transaction system, and an edit made to that file through Exegra is overwritten by the next import.
It reads no default source: the source directory is given with --source or as "source" in the import map, and the project with --project or with --map and --out.

data.name: Simulation contract
data.purpose: What a simulation engine is judged by: the engine input Exegra derives from the validated model for one scenario and fault set, and the trace format the engine must produce. A golden conformance suite holds an input and a reference trace for every shipped scenario.
responsibilities: Derive the engine input from the model: the scenario, its behaviors with variables, states and transitions, the events and the faults, with expressions as strings, so an engine needs no knowledge of JSONC, the meta-model or validation
Define the trace format field by field, with a format version
Run any engine against the golden suite, in-process or as a command reading an input on stdin and writing a trace on stdout, and report the first differing step and field

Give an implementation-level behavior the declared types of the references its expressions read (behaviorTypes: time as i64, each variable repr, each received payload field, lowered so a timestamp is i64, a duration u64, a declared id or scalar its representation, an option or optional field option), and name the time unit of a machine (machineTimeUnit)

Derive the machines a quota pool runs as (src/core/pools.js, WG-5278): one per pooled limit and modelled member, <pool>-<limit>-m<k>, with subject the pool's holder, states normal and throttled and the pool variables; usage is admitted on headroom, or within the fair share when throttled; a window end throttles a member over its share for the stated consecutive windows unless its exemption applies from that window, releases after the stated windows under, resets a rate and advances the window; an exemption is recorded the first time it is set, and lifts a throttle only when retroactive. simulationInput adds the machines of the pools a scenario lists after its behaviors, and the trace check and the proof plan count them among the scenario's machines
unknowns: Engine input and trace format 2 (contracts engine-input-v2 and trace-v2) are derived by simulationInput whenever a specification uses a format-2 construct (needsFormat2, simulationInputV2 in src/core/sim-input.js) and run by the engine's version-2 semantics (engine/exegra-engine/src/lib.rs dispatches on the version). Not yet: format-2 goldens (tests/conformance/goldens holds version 1 only), and the WG-4741 items: crash-instance, meters and the cost metric in the engine, and calibration, sensitivity, the operating envelope and revision binding of metric claims. A specification that uses no format-2 construct still derives version 1, unchanged.

The machines a quota pool runs as are derived, not entities: renaming a pool does not rewrite claim expressions that name them, and the simulator panel and inspector list only declared behaviors (WG-5281).

Present the active destination as a bottom sheet with peek, half and full detents on a phone: dragged on its header by touch or pointer, a flick snaps one detent on, a tap on the handle cycles the detents, tapping the active destination again or Escape collapses it, one sheet at a time

From 768 px show the active destination as a side panel beside the scene with a collapse control and a width dragged on pointer devices; from 1200 px show the explorer as a column of its own and the context panel beside the scene without opening anything
Use the same panel elements at every size: layout.js only sets data attributes and widths, layout.css places them, sheet.js drags the detents

Bring the inspector forward when an entity is selected by any route, unless another panel is pinned open: at peek on a phone when no sheet is open or another only peeks, docked on a tablet when the side panel is closed
Keep the scene interactive above or beside every panel, and dock the simulation transport above the navigation while a scenario is loaded
Give every interactive control a touch target of at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels and respect the safe-area insets of the device
Remember the context destination, the panel widths and the open state of the tablet and desktop panels in localStorage; a phone always starts with the scene and no sheet open
Keep the page frame from scrolling: html, body and the app frame clip their overflow, programmatic focus never scrolls, and only the inside of a panel scrolls

State the fault model in the scope of every claim evaluated under it
Relate scenario faults to the failure modes they realise

implementation.notes: formal/Exegra/Explore.lean: State (fault mask and Config, with decidable equality and hashing), successors, Reachable, the explorer explore with a Std.HashSet visited set, and the theorems step_mem_successors, explore_sound and explore_counterexample_real, whose axioms are pinned with #guard_msgs. The file sits inside formal/, which formal-semantics also declares. formal/Exegra/Search.lean: the generic breadth-first search over a node type with search_sound and search_counterexample_real. formal/Exegra/Temporal.lean: the forms, the monitor, runs (runRec), the product system, tcheck, tcheck_sound, tcheck_counterexample_real, tverdict and the exegra-lean temporal protocol; axioms pinned with #guard_msgs.

data.name: Exhaustive explorer
data.purpose: Explores every configuration of a scenario reachable within a bound, over every order of delivery of simultaneous events and every subset of the scenario's faults, with state deduplication. It reports that a state invariant holds in all N of them or returns a counterexample run, and it checks the temporal claims never, precedes and eventually on every complete run (a run ends at quiescence, at the step limit or in a failed step) by searching the product of the explorer's state with a small monitor. The explorer is defined in the Lean semantics and proved sound there; a faster explorer in the Rust engine (WG-4650) is to be checked differentially against it.
responsibilities: Define the nondeterminism a scenario admits as a successor relation over configurations: which of the pending entries with the head's time is delivered next, and which subset of the scenario's faults acts in the run; the deterministic step is one of the successors (step_mem_successors)

Explore breadth-first with a visited set under a bound on steps and a budget of states, and return holds with the number N of distinct states visited, a counterexample (a fault choice and delivery choices), or incomplete when the budget runs out

Prove that holds means the invariant holds in every state reachable within the bound (explore_sound) and that a counterexample is a run of the successor relation within the bound that ends with the invariant false (explore_counterexample_real), with only Lean's standard axioms
Report "verified by Lean for all N configurations within the bound" distinctly from trace-level checks

Define the temporal forms never, precedes and eventually over finite runs of the successor relation exactly as checkTrace reads them on a trace (a matcher is a delivery of an event or a firing of a transition; precedes allows the first event in the same step as a transition; eventually reads its expression in the final configuration of the run), and check them with a generic breadth-first search (Search.lean) over the explorer state with a monitor (Temporal.lean)

Prove the monitor agrees with the trace-level definition of each form (never_monitor, precedes_monitor, seen_monitor), that the search replays real runs (greplay_nodes), that holds means the form holds on every complete run (tcheck_sound) and that a counterexample is a real run that violates it (tcheck_counterexample_real); paths cut off by the bound or the state budget, and runs that end without quiescence and would violate or cannot decide an eventually, are reported incomplete, never holds
unknowns: The engine input (format version 1) carries no bound of a scenario's fault model, so every subset of the scenario's faults is explored; the concurrency bounds of fault models are not applied yet.
A fault acts for the whole run or not at all: a fault without an occurrence cannot act on some deliveries of its event and not on others.
Breadth-first order makes a counterexample one of the fewest steps, but that is not proved.
The Rust explorer for large state spaces is not built yet (planned: WG-4650); it will be checked differentially against this one.
Evaluation errors and failed steps end a path without being reported as such: a configuration whose invariant cannot be evaluated counts as a violation, and a failed step has no successor.

Format 2 inputs are not explored yet (planned: WG-4664, WG-4715). The specified relation adds internal entries to the simultaneous-order choice, the new fault kinds to the mask, and one successor per choice value and per instance of an any route; sampled draws are fixed by a seed named first in the result, and a result is shown as verified only when the scenario has no sampled site. Scenarios with workloads need a short horizon and maxArrivals, and keyed populations of thousands of clients are beyond reach. When a timed fault acts is not explored (WG-4704).
Temporal claims are checked without the claim's negatives and without the trace check's vacuity rules (a never whose matcher cannot occur in the scenario holds here without a note).
A violating prefix of a never or precedes claim is reported as the counterexample, not extended to a complete run; any extension violates it too, but that is not a theorem.
