implementation.notes: A Lake project (Lean 4, toolchain pinned in formal/lean-toolchain, standard library only): Exegra/Value, Json, Number, Expr, Input, Trace and Semantics define the semantics, Exegra/Properties proves its properties, Main is the exegra-lean executable (engine input JSON on stdin, trace JSON on stdout). npm run build:formal runs lake build in formal/; formal/.lake/ is build output, ignored by git and outside the traceability surface. tools/differential.js compares the native Rust engine with exegra-lean on the goldens and on seeded inputs from tools/gen-engine-inputs.js. Exegra/Impl/ is the implementation the application runs: Impl/Expr.lean (the numeric fast evaluator, eval_numeric), Impl/Json.lean (the in-place writer, write'_eq), Impl/Semantics.lean (the compiled format-1 engine) and Impl/Refinement.lean (runAnyValue_eq and runAny_eq, axioms pinned with #guard_msgs). Expression parses are kept in Thunks: Thunk.get is Lean's memoizing primitive, logically x.fn (), and the implementation declares no implemented_by, extern or csimp of its own.

data.name: Formal semantics (Lean 4)
data.purpose: The definition of the behavior language: the engine input, configurations, the expression language and the step relation, written in Lean 4 as an executable reference that the Rust engine is checked against, with its basic properties proved.
responsibilities: Evaluate a run to a trace in the documented format
Prove determinism of the step function, at most one fired transition per behavior per step, and termination under the step limit
Serve as the reference for differential checking of the Rust engine on goldens and generated inputs

Run, as the engine of the application (engine.run and exegra-lean), the implementation Exegra.Impl (formal/Exegra/Impl/): expressions parsed at most once per run, arithmetic evaluated on unboxed floats, a step counter instead of measuring the list of steps, and an in-place JSON writer; Exegra.Impl.runAnyValue_eq proves it equal to the definition Exegra.runAnyValue on every input, so the theorems about the definition hold of what runs
unknowns: Format 2 is defined in formal/Exegra/Format2.lean for the constructs built so far (instances, routes, resources and resource faults, windows, workloads, links, timers, request lifecycle and measured outputs); formal/Exegra/Resource.lean proves the held-units and queue-bound invariants of a settled resource, the strict FIFO queue of a collapse included. Not defined yet: crash-instance with incarnations, meters and cost (planned: WG-4741).

lift_agrees is stated in formal/Exegra/Lift.lean with its proof left as sorry (pinned on sorryAx); it is checked differentially by tools/differential.js --lift on every liftable golden and generated input (planned: WG-4664).
The determinism property over seeds is not stated as a theorem for format 2 yet (planned: WG-4741).

Exegra.Impl optimizes format 1; format 2 runs the definition's step semantics (V2.traceOf) with only the fast JSON writer, so its expressions are still parsed at every evaluation (planned: WG-4798). Exegra.Json.parse is a partial definition, shared by the definition and the implementation, so it is outside every theorem (planned: WG-4797).

implementation.notes: formal/Exegra/Core/LTS.lean (the theory), Calculus.lean (the guarded-command calculus), Search.lean (the bridge from Exegra.Gen.search), Examples.lean (positive and adversarial examples: counter_le, ne_neg_one_not_inductive, ne_neg_one_invariant, bounded_not_unbounded, vacuous_false, mod3_in_range), Behav.lean (the behaviour calculus of M2.1: typed values, arithmetic sorts and expressions, transitions, Sys.lts, phase2_perm, phase2_perm_emitted, winners_nodup, deliver_perm, shaped_invariant, deliver_ne_shape, shape_unreachable, Expr.eval_fits), BehavExamples.lean (f4_ab_safe, f4_ba_safe, f4_next_reads_differ, f4_nonVacuous, f4Init_shaped, f4_ab_no_shape, divZero_counterexample, mod_truncates, typed_div_truncates, untyped_div_inexact, u8_overflow, emitted_inserted_by_time, emission_order_irrelevant); axioms pinned with #guard_msgs. The files sit inside formal/, which formal-semantics also declares. Checked by lake build in .github/workflows/check.yml.

data.name: Transition-system foundation (Lean 4)
data.purpose: The mathematical object every guarantee is a proposition about (docs/foundations.md, section 3 and milestones M1 and M2): labelled transition systems as relations, reachability, invariants with no bound on runs, inductive invariants, vacuity, bounded reachability, closed-set certificates, the bridge from the generic search to transition-system invariants, a minimal well-scoped guarded-command calculus over Int whose semantics is a transition system, and the typed behaviour calculus (machines, events, guards, effects) whose semantics is a transition system with snapshot reads and an explicit error state.
responsibilities: Prove unbounded safety from an inductive invariant (Exegra.Core.LTS.safe_of_inductive) and from a closed-set certificate checked by kernel evaluation (checkClosed_sound)
State vacuity explicitly: with no initial state every predicate is an invariant (invariant_of_no_init), so an invariant result is only meaningful together with NonVacuous
Distinguish bounded from unbounded results: an invariant is a bounded invariant at every depth (invariant_iff_all_bounds) and no single depth suffices (Exegra.Core.Examples.bounded_not_unbounded)

Carry results of the generic search to transition systems: a holds result is an unbounded invariant of every system the search covers (invariant_of_search) and a counterexample refutes the invariant of every system it is sound for (not_invariant_of_search)
Give the guarded-command calculus a semantics in which out-of-range variables cannot be written, updates read the state before the step (Cmd.exec_get) and steps are labelled by command

Give Exegra's behaviours (machines with control states and typed variables, events with payloads, guards, effects that set the machine's own variables and emit events) a typed calculus over Int, Bool and String whose semantics is a transition system (Exegra.Core.Behav.Sys.lts): references scoped by Fin, so a missing variable or machine cannot be written; integer arithmetic as format 2 computes it, each arithmetic node checked against the declared integer type format 2's staticTy gives it (operands and result, on every operator), % truncated and typed / truncating; division by zero, inexact untyped division, out-of-range operands and results and reads past the end of a state as errors, never default values or other values; a failing delivery leads to an explicit error state with no successor (err_deadlocked), and every system has an initial state (lts_nonVacuous)

Prove that under snapshot reads a delivery does not depend on the order in which its winners fire: the machines after phase 2 (Exegra.Core.Behav.phase2_perm), the emitted blocks up to permutation (phase2_perm_emitted), the winners of every step on distinct machines (winners_nodup), and the whole successor configuration, pending list included, equal in every order (deliver_perm), emitted entries being inserted by time in machine-index order as format 2's insertE inserts them; and show on the [a, b] / [b, a] example that snapshot reads give one verdict (f4_ab_safe, f4_ba_safe) where the calculus's model of today's next-configuration reads gives two (f4_next_reads_differ)

Prove that the shape of a configuration (one state per machine, a control state of the machine, one value of the declared sort per variable) is invariant from a shaped initial configuration (Exegra.Core.Behav.shaped_invariant) and that no step from a reachable configuration then fails with shape (shape_unreachable), and that the static sort of an expression is sound for evaluation (Expr.eval_fits)
unknowns: The guarded-command calculus (Calculus.lean) is single-sorted (Int) with no events, timers, faults or time. The behaviour calculus (Behav.lean) has events, guards and effects but no timers, faults, time bound, stopAt, random draws, payload literals beyond Int, Bool and String, or counted instances, and no static well-formedness predicate Sys.WF from which no step fails with sort (Expr.eval_fits is the lemma it will rest on; the shape of the initial configuration is a hypothesis of shape_unreachable); there is no executable scheduler, so step_sound and successors_complete are not proved, nor phase2_eq_par (the parallel closed form of phase 2), pending_perm_bisim or a renaming theorem giving one verdict for every listing in general; format-2 input is not elaborated into the calculus (the elaboration must give each arithmetic node format 2's staticTy), so none of these theorems is about the format-2 interpreter (Exegra.V2), which still computes with Float (milestone M2, increments M2.2 to M2.8 of docs/assessment/2026-11-26/plan-M2.md).

By construction the calculus computes format 2's value wherever it computes one (no differential check yet confirms it), but some format-2 values are errors in the calculus: untyped arithmetic with an operand or result outside 2^53 - 1 and untyped / with a remainder (format 2 computes an IEEE double), == and != across sorts (format 2 gives false and true), string +, and a payload field read at a sort it does not fit; there is no > or >= (encoding them as swapped < and <= changes which error is reported), the error reported can depend on the order of the winners, and entries have no target, so a format-2 entry addressed to one instance would reach every machine (M2.2 for targets, M2.4 for elaboration, M2.5 for differential checks of values and errors).
Steps are labelled by the position of the delivered entry in the pending list, which cannot express per-entry fairness; labels by entry are needed before liveness (milestone M5).
There are no runs, traces, observations, fairness or composition yet (milestones M5 and M6), and no k-induction (M4).
Semantic completeness (invariant_iff_exists_inductive) is over arbitrary predicates; inductive invariants expressible in the calculus's expressions need not exist.

implementation.notes: src/core/proof-export.js (pure) builds the exploration request, the Lean proof file and the per-claim results; tools/prove.js runs lake build, the exegra-lean explore protocol and lake env lean on the generated file (formal/generated/, ignored by git), with the modules' shared libraries (precompileModules) loaded; formal/Exegra/Prove.lean holds claimInv, decodesTo, the Lean term printer of an input and the explore protocol of exegra-lean. The command is exegra prove (cli/commands.js).

data.name: Proof export
data.purpose: Exports a scenario's engine input and its state-invariant and temporal (never, precedes, eventually) claims to a Lean file whose theorems state the verified explorer's result per claim, checks the file with Lean and reports each claim as verified (for all N configurations within the bound, or on every complete run), a counterexample run, or incomplete, with the axioms the proof uses. Proving invariants for every reachable configuration at every depth, by induction, is planned (WG-4686).
responsibilities: Build the scenario's engine input exactly as simulate does and collect the state-invariant and temporal claims that list the scenario and apply to it; a claim that names behaviors or an expression outside the scenario is reported not evaluable

Write formal/generated/<scenario>.lean: the engine input text, its decoded Lean term checked against it (input_decodes), and per claim a theorem explore env (claimInv expr) bound maxStates = result, discharged by native_decide
Check the file with Lake, loading the modules' compiled code, and report per claim the method lean-exhaustive, the bound, N, the theorem, the file, the axioms and what is trusted
Render a counterexample as simulate shows a run: the step list with the delivery choices, the active faults, and the request-log lines of contract events

For a temporal claim write the theorem tverdict form env bound maxStates = result (from the exegra-lean temporal protocol), whose meaning is tverdict_sound and tverdict_real, and render a violating run with the reason in the trace check's words
unknowns: Results are established by native_decide, so each theorem depends on an auxiliary axiom that trusts the Lean compiler and runtime. Kernel reduction (decide) is not feasible: the expression language's number literals go through Float.scaleB and the visited set hashes strings with String.hash, both opaque to the kernel.
The unbounded proof of an invariant (by induction over the step relation, with the explorer supplying counterexamples to induction) is not built yet (planned: WG-4686).
Claim results are reported by exegra prove only; evaluate and verify do not show them yet.
Negatives of a claim are not explored in Lean: prove checks that a claim holds on every configuration of its scenarios, not that its negatives violate it (WG-4711).

data.name: Contract conformance
data.purpose: Lets an event be a request, a response or an error of a contract at a boundary, so that a simulated trace is checked and reads like a request log. Holds the type-string parser shared by the static and the trace checks.
responsibilities: Parse the type strings of payload fields and contract inputs and outputs (string, number, boolean, null, literals, unions, arrays); a type it cannot read is opaque and every value fits it
Derive from a contract the fields and error codes it allows for a request, a response and an error

Check a trace: for each step whose event is a contract event, the payload values fit the declared types, a request carries every input that is not optional, an error code is among the contract's errors, and a response or error answers an earlier unanswered request of the same contract (matched by the correlation field when the event declares one, otherwise by count); each violation is a failed automatic check carrying the step

Render a trace as request-log lines (src/core/contract-trace.js, requestLog): the contract's binding (method and path, or operation) or else the event name for a request, 'ok' for a response and 'refused <code>' for an error; steps that are not contract events give no line
Read traces and models only: the engine, its Lean semantics and the engine input format are untouched
unknowns: Object and generic types (for example {text, hash} or Operation[]) are opaque to the type check: their values are accepted unchecked.
A response is paired with its request by one correlation field or by count; there is no timeout or ordering rule for unanswered requests at the end of a run.

implementation.notes: The record and copy kinds are built-in meta-model kinds; the rules are hand-written in data-model.js and run from validate.js and claims.js.

data.name: Data model
data.purpose: Makes records, their fields, owning component, personal-data class, keys and the copies of them part of the specification, so that erasure, identity keying, shared-copy and freshness rules are computed over the model instead of read from hand-maintained tables.
responsibilities: Define the record kind (owner, key, fields with type, personal class, refersTo a record or the principal, role, retention) and the copy kind (of, fields, heldBy, scope, freshness, erasure, dependsOnAuthority), validated by the generic parser with positions
Check that a record's key and a copy's fields name declared fields, and that a numeric freshness or erasure bound has a unit

Compute the six data rules per copy, record and field: an erasure point on every copy holding a personal field or a principal reference; an erasure point or a bounded retention on every record holding a personal or credential field; no shared copy holding a principal reference, a personal field or authority-dependent data; party fields that refer to the principal by a non-name type; a freshness bound on every copy; a relationship path between a copy's holder and the owner of each record it copies
Report every finding as a validation warning naming the entity and the field, and evaluate the data-model claim method from the same findings
Answer the copies of a record and the fields a copy holds for the inspector and the Data projection
unknowns: A field counts as a name when its type text contains the word name or handle; there is no type system for field types, so a party field typed as an opaque string passes rule party-by-id (WG-4697).
Retention is free text: nothing checks that a record's retention and its copies' erasure points agree, and a copy of a copy cannot be declared, since of names records only (WG-4697).

implementation.notes: WG-4664 part of format 2: defined in Lean (Resource, Random, Format2, Lift), ported to Rust (v2.rs, random.rs), and checked differentially on generated version-2 inputs (tools/gen-engine-inputs.js --v2, tools/differential.js). Its claims stay not evaluated until recorded evidence supports them.

data.name: Resource model
data.purpose: Resources with capacity, request classes, queue disciplines and bounds, and the service demand of transitions: the part of format 2 that makes a pool, a connection limit or a CPU a queueing station.
responsibilities: Hold per resource its capacity, discipline (fifo or priority), request classes with priority, reserved units (at most the class limit), limit, queue bound and maximum wait, the overflow rule (refuse, drop, shed-oldest) and an optional load-dependent demand factor: a step table (the last row holds beyond it) or exact USL parameters evaluated at each grant

Record the use, acquire and release effects in phase 2 and apply them when the step settles: release, enqueue, grant by discipline and eligibility, then class bounds in declaration order and the resource bound; holdings are tracked per instance, resource and class, and release names its class

Draw service demand at the grant from the stream demand:<behavior>:<transition>:<effect> (effect index from 0), against the faults active at that time, and scale it once, rounding up, by the demand factor of the occupancy at the grant and by the combined scale-demand factor reduced to lowest terms (a part of 2^32 or more, or a service time of 2^53 or more, is a failed step); the service time is fixed at the grant
Delete a request's wait-timeout entry on every path that removes it (grant, bound refusal or drop, shed, crash), so a wait-timeout step always finds its request
Refuse statically a request whose units can never be granted, also after the fault mask is applied

Apply scale-demand, set-capacity, set-class-limit, collapse-classes and replace-demand, untimed or within windows through fault-edge steps, the value in effect being a function of the active set (last in the input's faults order, product for scale-demand, any for collapse), without preempting held units; return waiting requests to their own classes when a collapse ends

Apply crash-instance: an incarnation per instance, recorded on targeted, routed and from fields and on the instance's service-done and wait-timeout entries; at the crash remove timers, waiting requests with their timeouts and in-service requests with their service-done entries, release holdings, draw the restart time, broadcast notify; drop stale entries per behavior; restart edges restore only their own incarnation; a crash of a missing or down instance does nothing
Keep held units within class limits and capacity, and waiting requests within their bounds, as invariants proved of the step; deadlock freedom is not guaranteed and is left to claims and the explorer
unknowns: Built (WG-4664, WG-4729) in the Lean semantics and the Rust engine, resource faults included (set-capacity, set-class-limit, collapse-classes, scale-demand, replace-demand; untimed, or windowed through fault-edge steps), and derived from a specification's resources by simulationInput. crash-instance with incarnations is refused by both engines, and the grantable-units check is not repeated after the untimed fault mask (planned: WG-4741).
Processor sharing is not part of format 2; CPU is a FCFS multi-server station (planned: WG-4719).
Credit-based backpressure between components is not represented (planned: WG-4722); autoscaling and cold start are not represented (planned: WG-4720).

implementation.notes: WG-4715, in progress. Built: the integer lowering of distributions (src/core/distributions.js; every reference output of docs/simulation.md and the pinned SHA-256 reproduced, tests/core/distributions.test.js); open workloads (constant and Poisson by inversion of the integrated rate with exact integer square roots, phases, ramps, repetition, batches, clients picked uniformly or round-robin, payload literals, samples, weighted choices and counters, maxArrivals, the first-entry rule with a per-workload count of created instants) defined in formal/Exegra/Workload.lean and Format2.lean, ported to the Rust engine (workload.rs, v2.rs) and checked differentially on generated workload inputs (tools/gen-engine-inputs.js, tools/differential.js). Proved: an instant is always before the horizon (nextTime_lt_horizon) and a workload never creates more arrival entries than maxArrivals (makeInstant_arrivals_le).

data.name: Workload model
data.purpose: Workloads that drive a scenario from outside its behaviors: open arrival processes (constant, Poisson, ramp, step, on/off, attack floods) with client and address identities and payload generators, closed populations with think time, populations of client behaviors, links with bandwidth, latency, ordering and fan-out, and timers.
responsibilities: Generate open arrivals as instants of b entries, one future instant per workload in the queue, computed from the scheduled time of the previous instant when its original first entry is taken (a delayed copy is never first, and a per-workload count of created instants creates each instant once); draw, in this order, the instant time (Poisson, spent draws included), the batch size, then per entry the client and the payload fields; stop at the horizon

Validate phases (from < until, sorted, non-overlapping, repeat at least the last until; rates count instants) and schedule constant phases exactly, with j reset per phase and repetition, and Poisson phases (constant or ramp) by inverting the integrated rate against a unit exponential sample, with exact integer square roots and rounding to the nearest base unit: one draw per instant, no thinning and no rejection loop; refuse a phase whose mean interarrival is below 100 base units
Attach the request id, the client and the address; group users onto addresses by a drawn group-size distribution (sizes below 1 count as 1)

Run closed populations (issue with a workload-wide request counter, wait for the matching reply, think; a timeout ends the request with outcome timeout and a late reply is ignored) and population workloads whose clients are keyed instances of a behavior created at the start of the run

Send emits over links: FIFO transfer with time ceil(size * perSecond / bandwidth), then at link-done the latency draw, the delivery entry and the next transfer; ordered links deliver in send order; fan-out keeps one bounded queue per receiver at the link's full bandwidth and drops its oldest waiting message, never the one in transfer
Set, replace and cancel named timers by their stable id, so that a delayed timer is still cancelled

Lower specification-level rates, durations and distributions to integers and tables on unbounded BigInt: the exponential and normal quantile tables defined by integer algorithms (exp and ln in 96-bit fixed point, a 192-bit fixed-point normal CDF with bisection), equal to the correctly rounded values and pinned by the SHA-256 a23cd2a9566c106701375d5cf75ef982b8db6f3e52c199c47e6239649c840950 of their canonical text; log-normal sigma at most 8; a lowered value of 2^53 base units or more is a lowering error
unknowns: Built (WG-4715, WG-4729): open, closed and population workloads, address groups, links (bandwidth, ordering, queue bounds, fan-out, latency) and timers in both engines, derived from a specification's workloads and links by simulationInput (src/core/sim-input.js).
Packet-level networking and packet-rate floods are not represented: a link is a FIFO byte pipe with a latency distribution, one step per message (aggregated mode planned: WG-4718).
Matchmaking gather is writable only as a hand-written behavior (primitive planned: WG-4721).

implementation.notes: WG-4715, in progress. Built: the resource metrics of format 2 (utilisation as busy and capacity integrals and max held, queue length as integral and max, waiting time per request enqueued in the window with +infinity for a request removed without a grant or still waiting, nearest-rank quantiles at the input's exact decimals), defined over the step sequence in formal/Exegra/Format2.lean (Measured outputs), accumulated step by step in the Rust engine (v2.rs, Measure), output with the trace or alone with output metrics, and checked differentially on generated workload inputs. The request lifecycle, response time, throughput, outcomes, series, time-to metrics, meters and cost are not built.

data.name: Performance metrics
data.purpose: The measured outputs of a run as a pure function of its steps: throughput, outcomes, utilisation, queue length, waiting time, response-time percentiles, false positives, transition counts, link use and cost, per resource, class, link and boundary, over a declared window and in time series, all as integers; and meters, windowed measurements that behaviors read.
responsibilities: Follow the request lifecycle of docs/simulation.md: a request starts when its start entry is first taken as head, ends as error at once when that entry is dropped, crashed, stale or handled by no transition, ends at the first delivered end event with its key (delivered: head of a deliver step that does not fail), ends as timeout on a closed-client timeout, and is otherwise censored; count unkeyed starts, duplicate starts and late ends

Give ok requests the sample end - start and every other outcome and censored request +infinity; count samples as measured requests started, so a lost or refused request still counts; waiting time is one sample per request enqueued, +infinity when removed without a grant

Treat underpowered statistics by who starts the class: for open-started classes an underpowered run is left out and a null bucket skipped; otherwise both do not satisfy; time-to-recover always needs every bucket of its hold range non-null and satisfying

Integrate piecewise-constant signals over [warmup, horizon), with the value in effect at warmup and the last value held to the horizon, and the utilisation denominator the integral of the capacity in effect

Report nearest-rank percentiles, bucketed series on a grid that divides the window exactly, time-to-first and time-to-recover as durations t - after, and series aggregates max, min and mean; claims scoped to a phase or sub-window
Compute meters over (t - window, t] from the start-of-step configuration, with null for an empty window or a zero denominator and +infinity samples counted in quantile meters
Compute cost as counted quantities times exact rational prices, per price, in total and per bucket, for the cost aspect (WG-4669) to report
Mark a run truncated when it ended at the step limit, in error, or stopped with a measured request open
unknowns: Built (WG-4715, WG-4729): resource metrics; request classes with the request lifecycle, response time, outcomes, throughput, legitimate refusals (false positives) and transition firings, over the window and per series bucket, in both engines. Not built: link and cost metrics, waiting time per class, resource signals per bucket, time-to-first and time-to-recover, meters, and truncation by an open measured request (planned: WG-4741). Warm-up is declared, not detected.

implementation.notes: Built: the statistics (src/core/metric-stats.js: exact binomial tails and verdicts, the minimum run count, passes to hold and to fail, runs to decide, the sign-test interval, underpowered statistics, the margin, run seeds and the claim status with negatives; tests/core/metric-stats.test.js) and the metric-bound runner over engine inputs (src/core/metric-claims.js: one metrics-mode run per run seed through runEngineText, on the thread that evaluates claims, which in the application is the main thread). The method is registered and simulationInput derives format 2 for it. Calibration, sensitivity, asOf and revision binding are not built (WG-4741).

data.name: Metric claims
data.purpose: Claims over measured outputs, evaluated over many seeded runs with exact binomial and sign tests, reported with their sample count, seeds and confidence as model results (model-holds), never as verified or supported, and validated against recorded load runs.
responsibilities: Declare the claim method metric-bound: scenarios, metric (kind, subject, statistic, outcomes, window, series aggregate), op and bound, approx, or relativeTo another metric with its own window, fraction, confidence, runs, base seed, negatives (on the claim's scenarios or on variants declaring variantOf), control negatives and calibratedBy

Run the scenario once per seed, run r using the r-th SplitMix64 output of the base seed (mod 2^64), in metrics mode, and take one statistic per run; a truncated run does not satisfy the bound; an underpowered run is left out only when the engine input shows that open workloads alone start the class (computed from the workloads, behaviors, scenario steps and faults, never assumed) and the run had no duplicate starts, and counts as not satisfying otherwise; the test uses the thresholds of the N' runs kept

Decide model-holds, fails or inconclusive by exact rational binomial tails with N fixed in advance (the minimum N is the smallest with beta^N <= alpha, compared exactly); for approx, use the sign-test order-statistic interval of the median of the per-run statistic, which needs at least 6 runs at 95%

Report model-holds (never supported or verified) with the scope "model only; parameters as stated", runs, seeds, passes, N', fraction, confidence, the spread of the per-run statistic and the underpowered and truncated runs

Require each negative to fail and each control negative to hold before reporting model-holds; a base scenario that fails makes the claim violated; fixture results test the engine and method and are not evidence about any system

Check calibrations on hold-out load runs distinct from the fitting runs, with equal workload, capacities and window, a band widened over repeats, at least 6 kept runs and no truncated run, tolerance no wider than the margin computed from the beta-quantile of the per-run statistic, evidence not expired at the recorded asOf date and bound to the current component revisions; report unvalidated otherwise, and extrapolated outside the convex hull (exact rational linear programming) of the tested points with the same fault set
Vary every assumed and to-be-measured parameter over its declared range, one at a time and then pairwise among the flagged ones, and list first what flips the verdict
Refuse at validation a run count that could never hold, and a quantile or mean claim whose expected samples from declared open-workload rates are fewer than 30, per bucket for series claims
unknowns: Built (WG-4715, WG-4729): the metric-bound method is registered and evaluated on format-2 scenarios derived from a specification, reporting model-holds, violated or inconclusive with N, the passes, the fraction and the confidence, with negatives and control negatives. Not built: calibration, sensitivity, the operating envelope and revision binding (asOf is only recorded) (planned: WG-4741).

The status model-holds is implemented: it is a ClaimResult status of src/core/claims.js and the verdict of src/core/metric-stats.js, and metric-bound claims report it. Its final name and display follow WG-4703.

implementation.notes: Built (WG-4777). The producers live in the modules they observe; the server-side events are produced by tools/vite-plugin-exegra.js and returned with each answer.

data.name: Traffic recorder
data.purpose: Records the events a running Exegra really produces, named by the event ids of this specification (requests and answers of the persistence client with the development server's own events, change notices, engine-worker messages, commits, claim evaluations, simulator controls, preference and camera storage writes), as a bounded stream with logical sequence numbers, so that the stream can be replayed through this specification (component self-model-replay) and shown in the simulator panel's Live mode.
responsibilities: Keep the last 5000 recorded events in memory as {seq, id, payload, at}: seq is the logical sequence number (1, 2, 3, ...) and the only time the replay and the claim evaluator see; at is performance.now(), kept in the application layer for display and stripped before anything reaches the core (src/app/traffic-recorder.js, forReplay); older events are dropped and counted

Hand out request ids (nextRequestId), the correlation field requestId of the contract events of this specification; the persistence client sends it as x-exegra-request-id and the development server stamps its own events with it

Receive events from the producers at the code locations the event descriptions name: src/app/main.js (page, engine load, camera), src/app/session.js (project open, list and read, commits, saves and their answers, external changes, claim evaluation, simulator controls, preference writes), src/app/engine-runner.js (worker messages), src/persist/client.js (requests, the server events of each answer, change notices), src/ui/toolbar.js (export, import), src/ui/realisation-panel.js (generate), src/ui/layout.js (layout preference writes)
Record texts and bundles as their sha-256 (src/core/sha256.js), as this specification represents them, never the text itself

Record a write to a store that leaves the store's modelled abstraction unchanged (the selection and view of exegra.session, whether the explorer is open in exegra.layout) as nothing: a stutter step of the self-model
unknowns: The stream is kept in memory only and is lost on reload; there is no durable record under specs/<project>/.history/ (WG-4780).

The development server tells its own writes from external edits by the hashes it wrote. A change written by the server for another tab is therefore not seen as an external edit by this tab, and the replay reports its change notice as unpredicted (WG-4781).
Command-line runs (cli/commands.js) record nothing: the stream covers the browser application and the development server only.

data.name: Self-model replay
data.purpose: Replays a recorded stream of real events through the behaviors of a scenario of this specification (live-session), one event at a time, and reports every divergence between what the running application did and what the self-model allows.
responsibilities: Execute the behaviors of the scenario with the step semantics of the engine (phase 1 choice reading the configuration before the step, phase 2 effects in scenario order, the expression language of src/core/expr.js, the engine input of src/core/sim-input.js), delivering the recorded events in recorded order with their recorded payloads; logical time is the recorded sequence number

Keep the events the model emits as predictions instead of queueing them: a recorded event that some transition of the scenario emits must match a pending prediction of the same event (by its correlation field or requestId when both carry it, else the oldest); any interleaving of predictions that respects causality is accepted, because a real run interleaves independent chains (a network answer, a file-watch notice, a claim evaluation) in whatever order they happen

Report divergences under the claim real-runs-replay-through-self-model: an event that is not an event of the specification (unknown-event), an event the model emits but did not predict here (unpredicted), a predicted event that no behavior consuming it accepts in its current state (not-allowed), a recorded payload value that differs from the predicted one (payload; correlation fields and values the transition gives as number literals, which stand for counts the model does not track, are not compared; nor are arrays and objects), a prediction not matched within 200 recorded events or by the end of a closed stream (missing), and an expression of the model that fails on the recorded payload (error)

Calibrate instead of diverging when a predicted value reads a variable that no transition has written since the start of the stream: its declared initial value stands for the environment when the stream started (a file hash on disk, a stored preference), so it takes the recorded value; the step lists the calibration

Return the replay as a trace (steps with fired, ignored, responsible, configuration, the pending predictions and the divergences of each step) that checkTrace, requestLog, the simulator panel and the scene read like a simulated one
unknowns: The engine itself is not driven: it runs a scenario to quiescence and delivers simultaneous events in queue order, so the replay reimplements one engine step in JavaScript without faults. Agreement with the engine is by construction from the same engine input and expression language, not checked against the Rust engine.
A stream that starts mid-session (after the recorder dropped events, past 5000) is replayed from the declared initial configuration; divergences near its start can come from the missing prefix.

Divergences a longer real session still shows (WG-4782): the camera saved after a view switch with nothing stored is the camera the fit animation produced, not the last camera the model tracked (camera-keep); a restored camera is saved again with its last digit changed by the view's round trip (camera-apply); a commit that changes only comments or formatting re-evaluates no claims, while claims-on-commit predicts an evaluation for every change of the specification text (missing claims-evaluation-requested); a terminated engine worker never finishes its run, while engine-worker-flow still emits worker-run-done for it (missing).

implementation.notes: The Lean side (formal/Exegra/Api.lean, formal/Exegra/Api/) is the logic; src/core/lean.js and formal/wasm/glue.c are glue in the trusted base. Built into src/engine/lean/ (generated, not committed); downloads and checkout-independent objects are cached under %LOCALAPPDATA%\exegra\cache\formal-wasm (EXEGRA_CACHE_DIR overrides).

data.name: Lean call boundary
data.purpose: The one way the JavaScript shell calls the Lean core: a JSON request {fn, args} to a JSON reply {ok} or {error}, through the Lean core compiled to WebAssembly.
responsibilities: Keep the registry of callable Lean functions (Exegra.Api.registry): each module port lists its functions in its own file under formal/Exegra/Api/ and appends the list; the C glue, the exported symbol and the JS binding never change
Answer every request with a reply: an unknown function, a malformed request, a refusal and a trap are errors as values, and a trap discards the instance
Load the module synchronously in Node and after an awaited fetch in the browser or a worker (src/core/lean.js)

Build the module reproducibly from pinned inputs (npm run build:formal-wasm): emscripten 7.0.0, the Lean runtime at the toolchain tag with the committed patch, libuv v1.48.0, Init/Std C from the toolchain, Exegra C from lake; wasm64 only
unknowns: Stable Safari does not support Memory64, so the Lean core, and with it the engine, does not run there until Safari ships it (decision 2026-11-18). A wasm32 build would need its C from a 32-bit Lean compiler (spike/lean-wasm/README.md, wasm32 caveats).

The Lean engine is still slower than the Rust engine it replaced on the goldens, now mostly in reading JSON. Measured 2026-11-18 in Node 24 on Windows 10 (wasm64, best of 10 runs): live-session 17.0 ms (was 21.5 ms; Rust 1.95 ms), app-start-and-open 14.1 ms (was 24.1 ms; Rust 2.4 ms). Natively about two thirds of that is Exegra.Json.parse, a partial definition nothing can be proved about yet; a fast parser proved equal to a total definitional parser is WG-4797. Format 2 runs the definition's step semantics, with its expressions parsed at every evaluation (WG-4798). Loading and initializing the module takes about 119 ms once per process.

data.name: Rust engine (differential oracle)
data.purpose: The former simulation engine, the Rust crate engine/exegra-engine, kept as an independent implementation the Lean engine is compared against: as WebAssembly in the conformance tests and as the native exegra-sim in the differential check.
responsibilities: Reproduce every golden trace, as WebAssembly (tools/rust-engine.js) and as the native binary
Give byte-identical traces to the Lean engine on the goldens and on generated inputs (tests/core/conformance.test.js, tests/core/formal-semantics.test.js)

implementation.notes: Run by hand when the Markdown file changes; one way, as the Markdown importer.

data.name: Register importer
data.purpose: A command line tool that converts one large Markdown specification file, written as headings, prose and register tables, into the specification file of a linked project: every table row becomes an entity of a kind the import map declares (or a generic table row), and every entity names the line it came from.
responsibilities: Read one Markdown file and the project's import map (specs/<project>/import-map.jsonc with "format": "register"), which declares the entity kinds, the table rules (header cells, optional heading scope, the id column or id prefix, a property per column, reference columns), component categories and aliases, and which identifier patterns count as mentions

Hold every line: headings become sections whose bodies keep prose verbatim, and each imported table row and table header is replaced in its section body by one {{entity:<id>}} marker line; write nothing unless the file rebuilds line for line with each marker expanded to the lines it came from
Make every row entity render back to its cells: a row rendered from its properties must give the same cells as the source row, or the import fails naming the entity

Give every imported entity a source property (path:line in the source repository) and, when the row carries an identifier, a ref property with the identifier as written; identifiers and citations named in a row become its mentions (references to imported entities) and citations (as written)

Record what it recognised but could not map (a row whose cell count differs from its header, an unresolved mention, a duplicate identifier, a reference column naming no entity) as losses with counts and examples, printed and written into the generated specification's system notes

Merge the draft fragments the map lists ("drafts"): authored entities that are not from the Markdown, each given origin "draft" and the file and line of its declaration as source, citing in basis the imported entities it answers; drafts never change the Markdown the sections render
unknowns: It writes the project's specification file directly with node:fs, not through the workspace service or the transaction system, like the Markdown importer; once a map says "authority": "jsonc" it refuses to import over that file (only --out writes elsewhere), so edits made in Exegra are not overwritten.
It does not analyze or validate what it writes; that the output analyzes without errors is checked by the tests and by exegra validate.

data.name: External realisation
data.purpose: Lets a project be realised in other repositories: reads the realisation roots a project's project.jsonc names, checks modules declared in a root against that root, and turns a root's JUnit reports into pass, fail or not-run results for test evidence that points into it.
responsibilities: Resolve the roots of project.jsonc (alias, path relative to the project directory or absolute, include and exclude globs, test runs, environmental patterns) and refuse a malformed declaration
Check a module written <alias>:<path> against that root, report a module naming an undeclared alias as missing, and report unclaimed files only for a root that declares include globs

Through `verify`: run each test command a root declares (unless --ingest-only), then read its JUnit report, and record each external test evidence as pass, fail or not-run by matching file, describe path and test name
Record a test as not-run, never as failed, when it is absent from the report, skipped, reported as an error, or failed with a message matching the root's environmental patterns
unknowns: Only JUnit XML is read; a root whose runner cannot write JUnit cannot provide test evidence.
Results are not tied to the commit of the root they were recorded from (WK-393 follow-up).

data.name: Root test runner
data.purpose: The test runner of a realisation root (bun test, for example), started by `exegra verify` through the command project.jsonc declares for that root, writing a JUnit report.
responsibilities: Run a root's tests and write a JUnit XML report

implementation.notes: formal/Exegra/Integrity.lean: Facts (a search tree), Term, Formula (with relation atoms), Sat under an interpretation (the meaning), eval and eval_iff, refutes and refutes_sound, Facts.find_complete, cex; derived relations: Program, Least (the impredicative least-model meaning, stratum by stratum), solve (the fixpoint checker with fuel), wf and posF (stratification, decided by the kernel), sat_mono, stratum_closed, stratum_le_closed, least_eq_table, holds_of_eval and violated_of_refutes; the exegra-lean integrity protocol; axioms pinned with #guard_msgs. The commands are exegra integrity and exegra prove-integrity (cli/commands.js).

data.name: Integrity rules
data.purpose: Declarative consistency rules over a whole specification (the built-in integrityRule kind), with derived relations defined by recursive clauses (the built-in integrityRelation kind, stratified Datalog with a least-model meaning), evaluated on every edit with counterexamples, enforced by the transaction system as a ratchet, and proved or refuted in Lean with kernel-checked proofs.
responsibilities: Parse a rule of the rule language: forall and exists over the entities of some kinds, all entities, or the values of a term, with an optional where filter; property access that follows references through lists; kindof; ==, !=, in, not in, nonempty; !, &&, || and =>; string, number and boolean literals and literal sets; and atoms rel(t1, ..., tn) of derived relations. No arithmetic, and relations range over finite candidate tuples, so evaluation is total
Check a rule statically: every variable bound, every kind declared, every property declared on some kind; an invalid rule is a validation error

Check the derived relations (the built-in integrityRelation kind: params ranging over entity kinds, clauses in the rule language) and stratify them: the strata are the strongly connected components of the dependency graph in topological order, and within a component every atom of the component occurs positively (! flips, the left side of => flips, a forall filter flips, an exists filter does not). Negative recursion (integrity.relation-unstratified), a wrong number of arguments (integrity.relation-arity), an unknown relation (integrity.relation-unknown), a free variable that is not a parameter (integrity.relation-unbound), a parameter kind that does not exist (integrity.relation-kind), a clause that does not parse (integrity.relation-syntax), malformed parameters (integrity.relation-params) and more than 100000 candidate tuples (integrity.relation-size) are errors that make the relation, every relation that uses it and every rule that uses it invalid

Compute each valid relation as its least model over the product of its parameter domains: stratum by stratum, lowest first, iterating the clauses from the empty table until nothing is added; only the strata of the relations the rules use are computed, each at most once per model; an atom holds when some choice of one value from each argument term is a tuple of the relation

Evaluate every rule of a model once (memoized per model): holds with the number of instances checked under its leading universal quantifiers, or violated with every counterexample as variable bindings with entity ids and lines; a rule whose quantifier ranges over nothing is reported vacuous
Report each violation as a diagnostic of the rule severity at the first entity it names (integrity.violated), left out of the blocking error count
Tell the transaction system which violations of error rules a transaction adds (the ratchet): a violation is identified by its rule and its bindings

Export a rule to Lean: only the entities it can reach and the properties it reads (through the clauses of the relations it uses, and the domains of their parameters), every value interned to a natural number, the entities whose ids are the kinds of exported entities when a formula takes kindof, the entities as a balanced search tree, the program of the relations it uses in stratum order and their tables; write formal/generated/integrity/<rule>.lean with prog_wf (stratified), prog_solved (the checker reaches this table) and holds (proof by reflection) or one refutation per witness, each by decide +kernel and each about Sat under the least-model meaning Least

Run exegra prove-integrity: the Lean checker (exegra-lean integrity) must find the program stratified and solved, its relation tables must equal the JavaScript tables, and it must agree with the JavaScript evaluator on the verdict and every counterexample; Lean must accept the file, and every theorem may depend on the standard axioms only; each Lean process runs under a time limit (--timeout, default 300 s) and a rule whose relations have more than --max-candidates candidate tuples (default 500) is not sent to the kernel; otherwise, or past a limit, the rule is incomplete
unknowns: Property access reads top-level properties of entities only: a nested object property such as implementation.status or evaluate.method cannot be addressed (follow-up of WK-396).
Entity ids written as literals in a rule are not references: a rename does not rewrite them and a delete does not see them (follow-up of WK-396).
Undo, redo and reload are not checked by the ratchet: they restore or adopt text that was valid before, and may bring back a violation.
The Lean facts are exported by JavaScript: that they are the specification is checked differentially (exegra-lean integrity against the evaluator), not proved.

Derived relations are evaluated by naive iteration: every candidate tuple of the product of the parameter domains, each clause through the general formula evaluator, with no semi-naive evaluation and no indexing of atoms. Relations above 100000 candidates are refused, and a relation over Exegra's own relationships and components would slow every edit, so Exegra's own specification declares none yet; the examples are in tests/fixtures/integrity/relations.jsonc (WG-5267).

data.name: Reader pages
data.purpose: Derives the page of a reader view from the model and the view's reader blocks: text, counts by a classified property, tables and lists with grouping, facets and conditions, document sections with the tables their markers place, and an index of kinds. Knows no particular specification.
responsibilities: Resolve each block of view.reader.blocks into plain page data whose every row, count and section is an entity of the model
Classify a text property by the block's rules (first matching pattern wins) into a value, a label and a tone
Follow dotted paths through references and nested objects for grouping, columns, facets and conditions
Split a section body into prose and the tables its {{entity:id}} markers place, and list a document's sections in reading order
Give a view without blocks the system's description, an index of its kinds and the outline of its first document, and give each kind a page of its own
unknowns: Pages are derived in full on every scene change; a very large kind is cut to the first 300 matching rows on the surface, not paged.

data.name: Reader surface
data.purpose: Shows the page of the current reader view in place of the scene, with the scene's controls and overlay hidden, and turns every entity on it into a link that selects the entity through the session, so the inspector shows and edits it.
responsibilities: Replace the scene while the current view uses the reader projection and give it back otherwise
Draw text, counts, tables, lists, document outlines and sections, and the index of kinds with a page per kind
Keep each view's facets, text filter, show-all choice, open kind and open section while the model changes
Mark the selected entity on the page without redrawing it, and redraw on scene and project events
Link refs written in prose (an entity's ref property) to their entities
unknowns: Filters live only in memory; they are not remembered across reloads.

implementation.notes: Called by the parser (src/core/parse.js) as model.derive with {spec, metamodel, methods}: the document with every object as {"o": [[key, value], ...]} (members in source order, repeated keys kept), the meta-model and the claim method registry as data. The reply carries diagnostics and the model with raw paths ("3.0.12") and parts (node, key, start) for every location, and the semantic hash of the model. Differential evidence against the JavaScript it replaced: tests/core/model-kernel.test.js with tests/oracle/parse-reference.js.

data.name: Model derivation
data.purpose: Derives the semantic model from the specification's JSON document, in the verified kernel: the effective meta-model, the entities by kind with their data, every reference and expression, references resolved against the entities, and the meta-model's structural checks, with the diagnostic codes and messages of the JavaScript parser it replaced. Every location is a raw path into the document, which the parser maps to a source position.
responsibilities: Build the effective meta-model from the built-in meta-model and the vocabulary section (categories, relationship kinds, entity kinds with their sections and properties, properties on existing kinds, verification methods), reporting malformed, unknown and duplicate definitions
Check every section, entity and property against the effective meta-model and report each violation with its code, message, JSON path and raw path
Index every reference (properties of type ref, effects, claim evaluation parameters) and every expression with its JSON path, and resolve the references against the entities by id and kind

Follow the JavaScript semantics the parser had exactly: a map of members per object read on every access (property.duplicate each time), getNodeValue for entity data and the vocabulary, String() and template text of arbitrary JSON values

Prove what the model guarantees: with no reference diagnostic every reference names an entity of an allowed kind (Exegra.Model.derive_refs_resolve), and model.derive answers every argument (Exegra.Api.call_model_derive_total)
unknowns: Two differences from the JavaScript parser where Lean strings cannot follow: a lone surrogate in a string becomes U+FFFD before the call, and the label of a declared entity kind is lower-cased in ASCII only in the entity.type and id.missing messages. The JSON reply carries -0 as 0 and a number beyond the double range as null; the parser then takes entity data and the vocabulary from the syntax tree.

Recursion over the document is bounded by fuel (twice the document depth plus 8); no theorem states that the bound is never reached, the differential test (tests/core/model-kernel.test.js) is the evidence that it is not.
The id check implements the pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(-[a-z0-9_]+)*$ of src/core/metamodel.json in Lean; it does not read idPattern from the meta-model it is given (it only quotes it in the message).

data.name: Stable serialization and text digests
data.purpose: Deterministic JSON text for written files and command results (object keys sorted at every level) and SHA-256 of texts for recorded events. Output presentation, outside the verdict path.
responsibilities: Stable JSON stringification with sorted keys for generated files, traces and command results
SHA-256 of a text as lowercase hex, equal to the workspace's hash of the UTF-8 bytes

implementation.notes: src/core/hash.js is the binding only; it holds no hash logic. It imports the call boundary (src/core/lean.js) and nothing else from src/core.

data.name: Semantic hash binding
data.purpose: The JavaScript side of the semantic hash: passes a model that does not carry its hash to the Lean hash function through the call boundary, and returns the hash and the normal form to the callers of src/core/hash.js.
responsibilities: Call hash.semantic and hash.normalize at the Lean call boundary with the top-level declarations of a model that was not derived by parseSpec
Return the hash Lean computed with the model for a model derived by parseSpec, without recomputing it
unknowns: Not in the verdict path in the strict sense: a claim's result is stamped with this binding's hash, so a binding error would misstamp a result without changing a verdict. The stamp is compared with the Lean-derived hash only by the callers that use it (for example transactions' expectHash checks).

implementation.notes: Hand-written; run from validate.js and from the readiness command of cli/commands.js.

data.name: Generation readiness
data.purpose: Says what a code generator needs to know about data and interfaces (declared types, record constraints and schema versions, contract details and hand-written holes, the realisation of every requirement) and about the cross-cutting patterns requirements repeat (policies, validations, retentions, quotas, retries, audits) and about the user interface and its journeys (screens, forms, actions, live bindings, user journeys), and checks it: consistency rules that always apply, and readiness rules that are errors only when the specification sets system.generation.
responsibilities: Check the type entities (representation, enum values, struct fields), the record constraints (set-null needs optional, unique and index fields are declared, changes list versions 1 to schemaVersion) and that a construction requirement is named in the models property of some claim or names a construct in realisedBy, always as errors

Compute the readiness gaps (codes ready.*) of records, contracts, events, requirements and cross-cutting constructs, report them as validation errors when system.generation is set and list them for the readiness command otherwise

Give each type name the class an expression can use it as (bool, number, string, bytes, struct, list) and type an expression from the classes of its references, with the operator rules the evaluator applies

Check the cross-cutting constructs (policy, validation, retention, quota, retry, audit): exactly one target, references that resolve to declared inputs, outputs, payload and record fields, expressions that parse, stay in scope and type against the declared fields, durations, positive limits and attempts, rule parameters that fit the rule and the target

Check the user interface constructs (screen, form, action, liveBinding, uiScenario): route patterns that are well formed and unique, view-model inputs supplied by route parameters, form fields and action arguments that fill declared contract inputs with fitting controls and well-typed expressions over route parameters, view-model outputs and the principal, navigations that give exactly the target route parameters, refresh paths into the view model, and journey steps of one known kind each that name existing screens, forms, fields, events and browsers and select by WAI-ARIA role and non-empty accessible name only

Check the journey steps of user journeys and per-row actions: element selectors by role, exact or patterned accessible name, heading level and within; page title, attribute, count and absent-text expectations; raw-path and tenant-host navigation, reload, back and no-reload markers; request logs, direct API calls, cookie checks and replays; captured values defined before every ${name} use and captured once; emulation, overflow and placement checks; timeouts; and per-row actions over a view-model list of a declared struct, whose labels read only fields of the rows

Check the third set of user interface constructs: select and radio options taken from a view-model list (optionsFrom), at most one catch-all screen with no address of its own, navigation addresses and parameters that read query.<param> and form.<field>, live-binding conditions over the event payload and the view model (expressions, {value, in} membership, any and all), toast placeholders that read names in scope shown as text, derived form fields (derive, until edited, slug transform, no cycles), and action results kept in declared screen-local values of the same type instead of navigating

Check telemetry: the services of system.telemetry, each event's logging (an allowlist of payload fields that exist, are scalars, are neither marked sensitive nor of a sensitive type, and are written under names of their own, by a declared service under a unique log name, or not logged with a reason), that every domain event states its logging when system.generation is set, and that a journey's expectLog step names a logged event, its service and members of its line only

Check the fourth set of user interface constructs: request encoding on contract inputs (trim, split, as, empty), form initial values (a path, or the first item of a list whose field equals an expression), field normalization, second calls (then), view-model overlays on success, refusal prefixes and announcements, action confirmation announcements, alsoOn on every screen of one authentication, and error messages (by check kind or error code, placeholders that fit their kind, no two messages wording the same thing for the same forms and actions), with the default refusal message as a readiness gap when generation is set

Check that every value a scenario feeds a machine (a step payload, an inject-event fault payload) has the type its event declares: uuid format, integer bounds, enum values, required and undeclared fields, option fields (scenario.input-type, an error when system.generation is set, a warning otherwise)

Check the metadata model (src/core/tenant-data.js): once a type has metamodel tenant-schema every record states its scope, platform or tenant-meta (record.scope-missing); a record that names a tenant object type or carries tenant field values (an object-id or values type, or a map keyed by a field-id type) is a tenant-meta record and never a fixed platform record for tenant domain data (record.tenant-data-fixed); a tenant-meta record, and only it, is described by the tenant-schema type (record.described-by)

Check the language entities (src/core/language.js), and evaluate, check and print their expressions for function examples with the kernel's results, error texts and Display (src/core/language-eval.js, pinned by the shared case table tests/fixtures/language/kernel-cases.json): an expression language users of the specified system write, stated as an AST union, a value union, shapes, scopes and operators each bound to a primitive of the fixed catalogue pinned to the Strata kernel; operator names unique (language.operator-duplicate), no word or symbol claimed twice (language.token-clash), tokens of the right lexical class for their form and forms the primitive is written in (language.syntax), precedence and associativity on binary and prefix operators only, one associativity per level (language.precedence), primitives from the catalogue (language.primitive-unknown), operands agreeing with the primitive arity and the AST variant (language.arity), shapes declared (language.shape-unknown), null handling equal to the primitive's (language.nulls), operators naming variants and cases of the AST with at most one per variant or case (language.variant), scopes well formed and read (language.scope); with system.generation every AST variant and case has an operator and every operator a primitive (ready.language-variant-uncovered, ready.language-primitive-missing)

Check the function entities (src/core/function.js, src/core/function-syntax.js, src/core/function-value.js, src/core/language-eval.js): pure functions with typed parameters, a return type (the built-in unit for a function that gives nothing), an optional error union, lets and a body in the function body language (the guard language with field access, if, let, match, struct and union constructors, list literals, the unit value (), the JSON null where json is expected, variants and fields named like keywords written after a dot, as patterns and before a colon, map, filter, find, any, all, fold, sortBy (by a number, string, bool, enum value or a list, option, struct or union of those, ordered as Rust's derived Ord: lists item by item), take, concat, keys, values, get, insert, remove, format with the {} (Display), {:?} (Rust's derived Debug) and {:json} (serde_json text) placeholders, eval (with an optional lookup that following a reference reads), check and print of a declared language, the string operations startsWith, endsWith, length, trim, chars, snakeCase, parseTime and the ASCII character classes, call, fail and try); bodies parse (function.expr-syntax), name what exists (function.expr-reference) and type against the declared types (function.expr-type), matches are exhaustive (function.match-exhaustive), the call graph is acyclic but for structural self-recursion on a strict sub-value of a union parameter (function.recursion), fail and try use the declared error union (function.error-unknown), parameters, returns and lets are well formed (function.param), and every example is evaluated in JavaScript and gives its result or error (function.example-failed); with system.generation every function has a success example and one per error variant it can fail with (ready.function-example-missing)

Hold the built-in representation types (unit among them, the type of one value, which no id or scalar represents) and decide when a type name resolves: a built-in, a declared type, list<T>, set<T> or option<T> of a name that resolves, or map<K, V> of a key and a value that resolve, with type texts split at the comma outside angle brackets so generic types nest (map<K, map<K2, V>>, list<map<K, V>>)

Check the capability model (src/core/capabilities.js): every capability that a contract requires (auth.requires), a plan entitles, a role or grant confers, a delegation or token scope passes on and a feature flag gates is a capability (capability.unknown); with system.generation every contract that is not local requires one (capability.required); every capability is conferred by a role or grant and is core or entitled by a plan (capability.unreachable); a delegation passes on only what its source holds and a grant confers only what its issuer role holds (delegation.exceeds); grant and delegation durations are durations (capability.duration)

Check example fixtures (src/core/function.js, src/core/function-fixtures.js): exampleFixture entities declare a value of a type once, and a function example's argument, result or error may be {fixture: id} or {fixture: id, with: {dotted path: value}}, resolved before the example is evaluated; an undeclared fixture is refused (example.fixture-unknown), a fixture whose value is not its type or that, with its overrides, is not the type it stands for (example.fixture-type), and an override path that does not lead into the value (example.fixture-override)

Measure the branch coverage of function examples (src/core/function-coverage.js, WG-4965): with the evaluator's branch recorder attached, every example is evaluated and each branch it takes is recorded (both branches of if, each match arm, the value and error paths of try, fail); with system.generation every branch of every function is taken by some example (ready.function-branch-uncovered, one gap per function naming each branch with its line and column; not for a function that misses an example or has one that fails, nor while any function has a finding; severity info when system.generation.functionBranches is gap)

Check union, map, set and constraint types (src/core/type-shapes.js): a union has named variants whose fields resolve (type.union-variants, type.union-field), a newtype variant has one field and a tuple variant two or more positional fields, none optional, its wire encoding (external, internal, adjacent or untagged tag, tagField, contentField, variantCase) agrees with its variants, an internal tag writing no newtype or tuple variant, an untagged union with no tag field, content field or variant case, no two variants written as one JSON shape and a json newtype last (type.encoding), a map key is a string, an integer or an id or scalar over one, also inside a list, set, option or another map (type.map-key), a struct does not contain itself through struct fields alone (type.recursion), and constraints (pattern, minLength, maxLength) sit only on an id or scalar whose representation takes them (type.constraints); a union or map value has the opaque class of json and a set the class list in guard expressions, and a scenario value of a set type repeats no item

Check derived and facade contracts (src/core/derivation.js): a derivation exactly on a contract with realisation derived, of kind pure, read (optionally with a need loop, insufficient and needRounds together) or command with the fields of its kind, and optionally header: true, the load with no needs first, whose outputs the needs function reads, then the needs loaded in one round no need round counts (derivation.kind); functions whose parameters are inputs (or load outputs) of the same name and type, whose results are the outputs and whose error variants are errors of the contract, an insufficient-state variant carrying one need, a fault error without payload (derivation.signature); a load contract that is not a target and whose inputs are filled from the inputs and the needs and whose outputs and errors fit (derivation.load); a commit contract that is not a target and whose inputs are filled, whose conflict error exists and whose outputs and errors fit (derivation.commit); need rounds and conflict retries as non-negative integers (derivation.bounds); a facade with no implementing component whose bffRoute method, path and shape exactly one served contract (not a facade or a target) states (contract.facade-route); with system.generation every function a derivation names is declared (ready.derived-function-missing)

Check supplied inputs (src/core/supplied-inputs.js, src/core/ui.js): binding.suppliedBy names declared inputs of a contract and says each comes from the route or the session (contract.supplied-by), never from the body, so no form field or argument and no action argument fills one (form.supplied-input, action.supplied-input), and a form or action need not fill it

Write and read the wire form of values (src/core/wire.js): every union tag (external, internal, adjacent, untagged), newtype and tuple variants, variant case and wire-cased field names, so a value round-trips through its JSON; and run a read or command derivation against a store (runDerivation in src/core/derivation.js), reporting the loads, need rounds and conflict retries
unknowns: Only the data and interface rules exist here; the rules for implementation-level machines and refinement are added by their own tasks under WG-4838.
The cross-cutting constructs are checked, but no generator turns them into code yet (WG-4838).
The user interface constructs are checked, but no generator builds the frontend kernel or end-to-end browser tests from them yet (WG-4838).

A language entity is checked here but not mirrored in Lean: its claims are checked by tests, not proved. Generating its parser, printer, checker and evaluator is specc's work (WG-4931); stating the Strata kernel language in Strata's specification is WG-4930.

Derived contracts are checked by shape, names and types here; whether a derivation means what the contract's postconditions say is not checked by Exegra but by tests of the generated code. Emitting their implementations is specc's work (WG-4935, Strata side).

A function is checked and its examples are evaluated here in JavaScript, but functions are not mirrored in Lean: their claims are checked by examples and tests, not proved. Compiling functions into a pure crate is specc's work (WG-4934). The JavaScript evaluator of a language follows a reference (through) only through a lookup an example supplies, which keys a reference by its field name alone; the case table states what the kernel does without one.

implementation.notes: Run by the cover-machines command of cli/commands.js.

data.name: Machine coverage
data.purpose: Measures which transitions and guard outcomes of each shipped implementation machine the specification's scenarios exercise, searches for event sequences that reach the rest, and reports a transition nothing reaches (docs/coverage.md, WG-4965).
responsibilities: Select the implementation-level behaviors whose realisation is shipped (src/core/realisation.js) and list their items: each transition that is not faultOnly, and the true and false outcome of each guard

Read the items a trace exercises: a fired transition and its guard true; the guarded transitions of the same state and event declared before it, false; every considered guard of an event ignored with reason guard-false, false
Run the scenarios that list each machine and record which scenario covers each item

Search, for the items left open, a bounded breadth-first space of action sequences on the machine alone: deliveries of its input events (not those it emits itself) with representative payloads from the declared types (scenario values, guard literals and their neighbours, both bools, enum values, null for optional fields; one instance for an instanced machine), and waits past the time thresholds of time-reading expressions or to the next pending event; a coarse round first (control state, guard variables, pending event ids), then the full state with widening payload choice; bounded by actions and by engine runs per machine
Keep a greedy cover of the runs that covered something new as generated scenarios cover-<machine>-<n>, and turn them into CreateEntity operations of kind scenario tagged generated-coverage

Report a transition no scenario and no searched sequence reaches as machine.transition-unreachable (a warning, an error with system.generation), saying whether its source state is entered by no transition, the search exhausted its states, or it stopped at a bound
unknowns: The search is bounded and its payloads are representative, not exhaustive: a transition reported unreachable within the bound may be reached by a longer sequence or another payload; only the structural case (a source state nothing enters) is certain (WG-4965).
A guard outcome nothing reaches is listed as open in the report, not as a finding; deciding that the outcome is impossible (complementary guards) is left to the reader (WG-4965).

The verified explorer of formal/ (engine.explore) explores the interleavings and fault subsets of one scenario, not sequences of inputs, so the search runs the engine once per sequence instead (WG-4965).

data.name: SQLite (node:sqlite)
data.purpose: The SQLite database engine built into Node (node:sqlite, DatabaseSync), which holds specification stores.
responsibilities: Store tables in one database file, run transactions, and let several processes read one database in WAL mode while one writes

implementation.notes: A data file, not code.

data.name: Specification store
data.purpose: <spec>.sqlite beside a project's specification: the SQLite store of that specification (tables entity, trivia, ref and meta), rebuilt from the committed JSONC and never committed (.gitignore).

data.name: Specification store service
data.purpose: Holds a project's specification in SQLite with an exact round trip: the JSONC text is cut into verbatim rows, one per entity and one per stretch of text between entities, and the rows in position order are the text again, byte for byte.
responsibilities: Import: parse the text once with jsonc-parser and cut it into rows: one entity row per item of an entity section (the meta-model's sections and those a vocabulary's entityKinds declare), one row per other top-level value stored whole (system, exegra, vocabulary, a section with no entity kind), and trivia rows for everything between them (keys, brackets, commas, comments, whitespace, line endings, the text before the root and after it), so every code unit belongs to exactly one row

Index each entity row by section, id, kind and component, and record its JSON value, the sha-256 of that value, and the ids it references (also in table ref, indexed by target), from the model the parser derives
Record in meta the store format and version, the project, the semantic hash, the unit positions count (UTF-16 code units of the imported text) and the sha-256 of the text last synchronised

Refuse, with a StoreError and nothing stored, a text that does not parse, is not well-formed Unicode, or is not valid UTF-8, and any import whose rows would not export to the same text, which is checked inside the import transaction
Export: concatenate the rows in position order; write a file atomically, and refuse to overwrite the specification when it changed since the store last synchronised with it
Give the model, diagnostics and semantic hash of the stored specification by the same analysis as its text (loadModelFromStore)
Open every database in WAL mode, so several processes can read while one writes
