data.name: Specification layers
data.purpose: Reads a layered specification (WG-4989): the platform specification plus product files that import the platform's entities by id and add tenant metadata of their own, checked ahead of the verified kernel and analysed as one model with every location in its own file.
responsibilities: Read each product file on its own: syntax, the product header (id, name, imports.spec naming the platform specification, imports.entities naming the platform entities it uses) and its sections

Allow a product to declare only tenant metadata (ARC-113 of the platform): the entity sections records, types, screens, forms, actions, liveBindings, errorMessages, behaviors, events, contracts, roles, scenarios, uiScenarios, claims, evidence and capabilities (the one platform section a product adds to, D-6590), and the typed sections objects, policies, segments, settings, ledgerUnits, ledgerPools, ledgerLimits, mailTemplates, noticeTemplates, tokens, triggers, automations and operations; refuse every other section with layer.kind-not-allowed

Splice the product entities of the entity sections into the platform text at the end of their sections, keeping the platform text byte for byte, and have analyzeSpec derive and validate the combined model; the typed sections are not spliced

Map every location and JSON path the analysis reports back to the file it is in (loc.file names a product file) and restate the diagnostics a layered specification gives a meaning: an id the platform or another product declares (layer.redefines-entity), a reference no layer declares (layer.reference-unknown)

Check the imports: an imported id the platform does not declare (layer.import-unknown), a platform entity used by a reference, a type text or a capability list without being imported (layer.import-missing), a reference into another product file (layer.cross-product-reference), an imports.spec that is not the project's platform file (layer.import-mismatch); every refusal says what is wrong and what to do

Keep the platform's semantic hash the hash of the platform text parsed alone, so adding a product file changes neither it nor anything generated from the platform; report the combined model's hash as the layered hash

Refuse a product entity that claims what only the platform may have (layer.platform-power): a role at platform level or with anonymous, service or external holders, a contract that is public with the anonymous scheme, is implemented by a platform component or carries a realisation of generated, hand or derived, a behavior at implementation level, an event that is a domain event, an elapsed-time event or states a delivery guarantee, a capability that is core, a setting that is set at or locked by the platform level

Refuse two product files with one product id (layer.product-id-duplicate), a product entity id that fails the id pattern (layer.entity-id-invalid) and a section item with no id (layer.entity-id-missing)
Refuse a platform entity that names a product entity, by a typed reference, a type text or a capability list (layer.platform-references-product), so the platform never depends on a product
Take the product files as they are on disk when a project reloads (Project.reload), so a long-lived session shows the layered model of the current product files

Check each value of a typed section against the platform type its section maps to (src/core/layer-values.js, one table and one generic check: struct fields required and optional, union variants by tag, enums, lists, maps, ids by pattern and length, scalars by representation, the authoring text of an expression): a value of the wrong shape is refused with layer.value-invalid and a union value the platform union lacks with layer.outside-catalogue (the published catalogue of INT-153: trigger-event, automation-step, tenant-operation-step)

Refuse an entity id that is not in the namespace of its product, the product id with each hyphen replaced by an underscore and two underscores (layer.namespace-missing, D-6582), and resolve the names the typed values hold against what the product files declare: an undeclared name in the product namespace is layer.reference-unknown and a name another product declares is layer.cross-product-reference, which also confines a product capability to its product
Report a product capability as unreachable only when no role or grant confers it: installing the product entitles it, and a product file cannot add a plan (D-6590)

Parse and check the expression text of every typed value whose platform type is expr or expression (src/core/layer-expr.js: the grammar and static check of the tenant rule language, in the scope the value is written in: the fields of the object type it belongs to, the params an operation or an event binds, the roles of the platform and of the product, and what a reference hop may follow): a text that does not parse is layer.expr-syntax, a field the object type lacks layer.expr-unknown-field, a role nobody declares layer.expr-unknown-role, a param the scope does not bind layer.expr-unknown-param and a shape the operator does not accept layer.expr-type, each naming the product entity and the position in the text. The grammar and typing include the nine operators of the language: checked + - * on integers (a timestamp plus or minus an integer is a timestamp; Time + Time is refused, ms_between gives the difference), ms_between, days, hours, minutes, concat and text, with a - before a digit a sign only where no operand ends before it, and an operand of the wrong shape is layer.expr-type with the message "<op> does not accept a <Shape> operand". A step of an operation reads the id of an earlier create step as a param (D-6548). tests/core/layer-expr-drift.test.js probes every operator a language entity declares against this parser and compares it with the language checker on the shared case table, so an operator added to the language fails a test until layer-expr.js handles it (WG-5120)
Refuse an object type that has a field with a personal declaration and no retention rule (layer.retention-missing, D-6584)

Accept the product header members version (three whole numbers joined by dots) and platform ({min, below?}: a platform release, and a later release from which the product is not supported), and refuse a malformed one with layer.header-invalid, as specc does (WG-5174)
unknowns: The browser application opens a project without its product files: src/app/session.js builds the Project from the specification alone, and the workspace watcher does not watch product files (follow-up of WG-4989).
Whether a product's claims and scenarios are about its own entities is not checked; any claim or scenario may be declared in a product file.

The product sections are a fixed list in src/core/layers.js and src/core/layer-values.js; nothing yet generates the tenant bundle a product installs through the platform's install-bundle contract. The check does not parse the block text of a template. The scope of an automation's expressions is not known here (the params come from the triggers that start it and the outputs of its steps), so its fields and params are accepted and only its syntax, shapes and roles are checked.

data.name: Derivation cache
data.purpose: A persistent, on-disk cache of the stages of model derivation that run in the Lean kernel, so that repeated Exegra processes over the same specification skip them (WG-5636). It wraps derivation from outside: the cached value is what parseSpec and analyzeSpec compute, and a hit is observably identical to a miss.
responsibilities: Key every entry by the SHA-256 of the entry format, the package version, the content hash of Exegra's derivation sources (every file of src/core and of the Lean build in src/engine/lean, by path and bytes), the stage name and the stage's inputs: the specification text (for a layered project the text that already holds every product file's entities) and the options that change the result (claimsOnly). No modification time is read, so editing a specification, a product file, the file project.jsonc names or Exegra itself is a miss

Cache two stages: parseSpec (the model and its diagnostics, only when the text is usable) and the semantic diagnostics of analyzeSpec (only when analyzeSpec parsed the text itself, never for a caller's own parsed model)

Encode a stage's value faithfully as tagged JSON (Maps, Sets, objects without a prototype, -0, infinities, undefined, shared references and cycles) or refuse it and cache nothing: a value the encoding cannot reproduce exactly (a function, a class instance, a hole, an accessor) is computed every time

Store each entry in one file under the cache directory (EXEGRA_MODEL_CACHE_DIR, else model/ under EXEGRA_CACHE_DIR, else the user cache directory: %LOCALAPPDATA%/exegra/cache/model, $XDG_CACHE_HOME/exegra/model or ~/.cache/exegra/model), with a header that repeats the key, the byte count and the SHA-256 of the body
Write through a temporary sibling and a rename, so a concurrent reader sees a whole entry or none and two writers of one key leave one valid entry; a failed write is ignored
Treat an entry that is missing, truncated, altered, of another format or under another key as a miss and replace it, never as an error

Bound the directory: past EXEGRA_MODEL_CACHE_MAX_BYTES (default 512 MiB) delete the least recently used entries down to three quarters of the bound, and delete temporary files a dead writer left more than an hour ago; a hit refreshes the entry's recency
Do nothing when EXEGRA_NO_CACHE is set (to anything but empty, 0 or false), when the sources cannot be read or outside Node; EXEGRA_CACHE_TRACE=1 reports each hit, miss and store on stderr
unknowns: The evaluation of claims is not cached: it runs the verified engine, and a claims run still takes the time of its scenarios after the derivation stages hit. Measured on the Strata specification (about 10,000 entities): validate 13.9 s cold, 1.0 s warm; claims 16.4 s cold, 7.8 s warm.
The diagnostics of a validate hit are rebuilt as copies: their loc objects are equal to the entities' but no longer the same objects. Nothing reads the identity.

data.name: Claim strength
data.purpose: Says how strong the check behind each claim status is and whether what it reads is the platform's own entities: a static, deterministic analysis of the model that never changes a status (decision dec-claim-check-and-grounding).
responsibilities: Classify the check of every claim: holds-by-construction (a never, state-invariant or precedes claim that every value nominal transitions can give its references satisfies, or whose occurrence only fault transitions or guards that can never hold produce; naming the variables and the fault transitions), restated-scenario (a counter compared with a literal equal to the extreme its one scenario reaches), single-trace, explored (from supplied exploration results), refined, and the method-based checks structural, data-model, lean-theorem, sampled, test, evidence and none

Classify the grounding of every claim and integrity rule: bound, partly-bound, self-contained or not-applicable, from what the behaviors it reads are anchored to (a refined existing behavior, a record, a contract event, an anchored behavior) and the payload fields of contract-less events they branch on, or the kinds an integrity rule quantifies over; under a baseline an entity the change adds anchors nothing
Count claims by check and grounding, and integrity rules by grounding
unknowns: Exhaustive exploration results (exegra prove) are not recorded in a project, so a trace claim is reported as explored only when the caller passes them; claims, evaluate, the claims report and admit never do yet (WG-5280).

The value analysis ignores guards when it collects the values and states nominal runs reach and does not follow arithmetic or keyed instances, so vacuity that depends on them is not found; restated-scenario examines only a plain comparison with a literal.

Grounding is structural: an anchored behavior may still branch on a field that means nothing, and the expression language cannot read roles, capabilities or grants, so the access model reaches a behavior only through a contract's auth.requires.

postconditions: Two calls of simulationInput on the same model give identical documents
A specification that uses no format-2 construct still derives a version-1 input, unchanged
preconditions: The input was derived from a validated specification, or is a generated input of the version-2 generator

Every integer is within its bound (docs/simulation.md, Integers and bounds; distribution tables below 2^53, unitExponential below 2^72); a specification duration that is not a whole number of base units is a validation error, never rounded
No reserved name is used, ids of behaviors, resources, meters, links and workloads are distinct, and every reference resolves
Phases are valid: from < until, sorted, non-overlapping, and repeat at least the last until
Reserved units sum to at most capacity, each class's reserved units are at most its limit, and every request can be granted, for every fault mask the scenario admits
A keyed behavior's max is at least the sum of the counts of the populations on it
A seed is present when any element draws

data.description: The serialized authority of a project: specs/<project>/spec.jsonc, or the file that specs/<project>/project.jsonc names. When that file is a manifest listing part files (specParts, WG-5386), the authority is its part files, which sit beside it, and each write goes to the part files holding the changed entities (tools/workspace.js writeSpecText(), tools/spec-manifest.js planWrite(), and tools/spec-store.js store export, each part by atomic rename through a temporary file); the manifest itself is never rewritten. Written by the workspace service (tools/workspace.js write(), under a base-hash check and atomic rename, from the session and from exegra apply) and, outside any transaction, by the bundle import (tools/workspace.js importProject()), by tools/import-markdown.js (--out), by tools/import-register.js (--out, or the project it names), by tools/make-benchmark.js (specs/benchmark/spec.jsonc) and by tools/spec-store.js (store export, atomically through a temporary file, refused as store.stale when the file changed since the last import). Exegra holds no personal data: no field is personal and none refers to a principal.

data.rationale: The rules are checked by machineReadiness (src/core/readiness-machines.js), called by validate, so a generator can rely on an implementation-level machine being complete. Evidence is the core test: one fixture that breaks each rule once and gives exactly that one ready.* error, a fixed version with none, and the exegra and strata projects, which have no implementation-level behavior and so report none. The rules are the ready.* codes of docs/semantics.md; a machine is keyed by the whole key of its record, every key field in order, in storage.key and in instances.key (storage.key-whole, WG-4907).

Timers the implementation sets are compared with the model's timers when the model transition sets some and are internal to the implementation otherwise; a model guard or effect that reads another behavior reads it from the same trace, through the machine that refines that behavior when it does not run itself. With refinement.timeScale, the model reads the trace time divided by it and its timer delays are compared multiplied by it. A delayed emit of the model is realised only by a delayed emit of the implementation for the same event and the payload fields the model sets, delivered after the model delay times the time scale; a timer never realises an emit, and an undelayed emit for a delayed one, or the reverse, is violated (reason emits).

It is about the calculus, not about the format-2 interpreter.

Emitted entries enter the pending list in machine-index order, each after every pending entry of no later time.

data.statement: In the behaviour calculus, from an initial configuration of the shape of its signature (one machine state per machine, each with a control state of its machine and one value of the declared sort per variable), every reachable state has that shape, with no bound on runs.

data.rationale: Theorem shape_unreachable of formal/Exegra/Core/Behav.lean (review-M2.1, finding 9), from shaped_invariant and deliver_ne_shape: in a shaped configuration every machine, variable and control-state index a step uses is in range. The theorem rests on the shape of the initial configuration as a hypothesis; a static well-formedness predicate Sys.WF that implies it is M2.2's. BehavExamples.lean discharges it for the [a, b] example (f4Init_shaped, f4_ab_no_shape).
data.statement: In the behaviour calculus, from a shaped initial configuration no step from a reachable configuration fails with the error shape.

data.rationale: Theorem Expr.eval_fits of formal/Exegra/Core/Behav.lean (review-M2.1, finding 6). A typed context has a shaped snapshot, own variables of their declared sorts and a time within 2^53 - 1 (the sort of the time; the bound on time is M2.2's). Every arithmetic node checks its result against its sort and a payload field is checked against its sort when read, so the theorem needs no induction hypothesis on operands. No theorem yet uses it to exclude the error sort from well-formed systems (Sys.WF, M2.2).
data.statement: In the behaviour calculus, when the static sort of an expression is defined, every value the expression evaluates to in a typed context fits that sort: it has that sort, and an integer lies in the sort's range (an integer literal has the one-point range of its value, an arithmetic node the range of its arithmetic sort).

data.rationale: Theorem u8_overflow of formal/Exegra/Core/BehavExamples.lean (review-M2.1, finding 3, demonstration D3), by kernel evaluation. Each arithmetic node carries the sort format 2's staticTy gives it (Expr.lean:267-277), and both operands and the exact result are checked against it on every operator, as format 2's intResult does (Expr.lean:289-297). That M2.4's elaboration assigns staticTy is not yet proved.

data.context: A requirement is realised by code and verified later, so it cannot be verified when first written; rejecting it pushed requirements into other entity kinds outside milestone tracking.
data.decision: admit applies admit.new-claim-weak only to claims a model method can decide at specification time. A new claim realised by code (kind requirement whose method Exegra does not evaluate itself, a method declared in vocabulary.verificationMethods, or external-evidence) that names a milestone and is not-evaluated or inconclusive is admitted and reported under pendingRealisation. A new requirement without a milestone is the reason admit.requirement-without-milestone; another code-realised claim without one stays admit.new-claim-weak. Structural, data-model, integrity, lean-theorem and the other methods in the claim method registry stay under admit.new-claim-weak.
data.title: admit: claims realised by code are pending realisation, not weak

alternatives: Make vacuous trace claims inconclusive in the evaluator. Not taken: the trace does hold, and the status says what the evaluator found on it; the weakness is in what the check could have found, a separate axis, and changing the statuses would move many existing results at once.

Require an exhaustive exploration (exegra prove) of every new trace claim. Not taken for now: prove needs Lean and a build of formal/, and its results are not recorded in the project, so admit cannot read them. The explored check is the place a recorded result will raise a claim (WG-5280).

Detect vacuity by mutation: run every scenario with all faultOnly transitions enabled, or with generated payloads. Not taken: negatives already do the first, both depend on the hand-written scenarios, and the static analysis of the values nominal transitions can produce answers the question for every nominal run, cheaply enough for every admit.

Ground a claim through its subjects or its behavior's subject component. Not taken: every behavior names a subject, so that field cannot tell a machine that reads the platform from one that reads only its own payload (judge F1).

Count any reference to another behavior as binding. Not taken: a fold's machines would then bind to each other. A behavior binds only through a chain of reads that ends at a refinement, a record or a contract.

Read the access model directly from guards. Not possible: the expression language reads variables, payload fields, time and other machines only, so roles, capabilities and grants reach a behavior through a contract's auth.requires, and integrity rules are where they are quantified over.
data.consequences: Statuses do not change; the strength is a second view that admit enforces for new claims only. The value analysis over-approximates nominal runs (it ignores guards when collecting values and reachable states, and treats other values as unknown), so it does not report a claim that some nominal run can violate as holds-by-construction, but it misses vacuity that depends on guards, on arithmetic or on keyed instances. restated-scenario needs one run of the claim's scenario and is restricted to a plain comparison with a literal. Grounding is structural: an anchored behavior can still decide on a field that means nothing, and a contract event's payload is still supplied by the scenario. explored is reported only when the caller supplies exploration results (WG-5280).
data.context: A verified status says that an evaluator checked a claim within its scope; it does not say how much that check could have found. The Harbourline fold (WG-5265) added 76 claims through admit, all verified, and an independent judge found that most of them prove only the author's own state machines: invariants that only the injected fault transition can break, a bound that restates the count of its one scenario, guards decided by booleans and numbers written into scenario event payloads, and no behavior that refines or reads a real behavior, record, contract, role or capability (judge report F1, F2, F7, F8). A real platform that let an agent change a plan would leave every one of those claims verified.
data.decision: Every claim and every integrity rule gets two computed attributes besides its status, from a static, deterministic analysis of the model (src/core/claim-strength.js, claimStrength): its check, how strong the evaluation behind the status is, and its grounding, whether what it reads is the platform's own entities or only the claim's own inputs. They never change a status. claims, evaluate and the claims report show them. admit counts them for the whole specification before and after the change, and rejects a claim the change creates when its check is holds-by-construction or restated-scenario (admit.claim-vacuous) or single-trace (admit.claim-single-trace), or its grounding is self-contained (admit.claim-self-contained); each such reason carries acknowledgeable: true so that a caller can accept it explicitly. Existing claims are counted and never a reason.
definitions: check holds-by-construction: a never, state-invariant or precedes claim that no run without the defect can violate. Nominal transitions are those not faultOnly, plus the faultOnly ones a fault of the claim's own scenarios enables. For a state invariant, the expression is true for every combination of values its references can take in nominal runs: a variable assigned only by fault transitions, or by nothing, keeps its initial value; a variable set only to literals takes its initial value or one of them; two variables of one behavior that start equal and are always set together to the same expression stay equal; a state reference takes any state reachable from the initial state over nominal transitions. For never, and for the then of precedes, the occurrence can be produced only by fault transitions, or by nominal transitions whose guard is false for every such value. The result names the variables and the fault transitions. Examples: hl-chk-rx-continuous-renewal (clockRestarts == 0, incremented only by the fault hl-rx-renew-restarts-clock), hl-chk-wv-clock-from-receipt (clockStart and receivedAt set together from time), hl-chk-au-append-only (hl-au-edited emitted only by the fault hl-au-edit-allowed).

check restated-scenario: a state invariant that compares one numeric variable which nominal transitions change by an expression (a counter) with a literal bound, listing exactly one scenario, where the bound is exactly the extreme value the variable reaches in that scenario's run and the run changed it. Example: hl-chk-gf-no-creation-after-loss, featureRecords <= 1, where the one scenario creates one record. Only a plain comparison is examined; a bound inside an implication is not.

check single-trace: any other state-invariant, precedes, eventually or never claim. It is decided by running hand-written scenarios, without exhaustive exploration and without refinement. Example: hl-chk-ag-forbidden-refused.

check explored: a trace claim that an exhaustive exploration of its scenario (exegra prove) found to hold, when the caller supplies that result; exploration results are not recorded in a project yet (WG-5280). check refined: a refines claim, or a trace claim whose behaviors all refine an existing behavior.

Other checks name the method: structural (no-relationship, reachable, only-via, has-port, property-defined, acyclic, implementation-language), data-model, lean-theorem, sampled (metric-bound), test (external evidence with a test attached), evidence (other external evidence and external verification methods), integrity (an integrity rule) and none (no method, or one this build does not evaluate).

grounding bound: the check reads the platform's own entities: the component graph (structural methods), records and copies (data-model), Lean definitions (lean-theorem), the entities of the kinds an integrity rule quantifies over, or behaviors that are anchored and branch on no free input. A behavior is anchored when it refines an existing behavior, is stored in a record (storage or instances.storedIn), reacts to or emits an event of a contract (the details name the capabilities the contract requires), or reads the state or variables of an anchored behavior. Example: hl-agent-roles-hold-no-forbidden-power, which ranges over every role.

grounding partly-bound: some of what the check reads is bound and some is not: an anchored behavior whose guards or effects also read a payload field of an event that belongs to no contract, a claim that reads one anchored and one unanchored behavior, or a data-model claim restricted to records the change adds.

grounding self-contained: the behaviors the check reads are not anchored: their guards and effects read only their own variables, time and payload fields of events that belong to no contract, which the scenarios supply as literals. Example: hl-agent-forbidden-acts-flow branches on event.changesPower, so hl-chk-ag-forbidden-refused is self-contained.
grounding not-applicable: the status comes from evidence outside the model (external-evidence or an external verification method), or nothing is evaluated.

Baseline: under admit an entity the change creates does not anchor anything, so a new behavior reading another new behavior, or a new event of a new contract, is self-contained. claims, evaluate and the claims report have no baseline and count every entity of the model.
data.title: Claim check strength and grounding

alternatives: Region as a property of every entity (records and copies each naming a region): not taken. A record class or copy class has no single region; its data is wherever its holder runs, and a tenant's region is run-time data, so a region per record would be stated twice and drift from the placement of the component that holds it.

A separate placement relation (placement entities pairing a component with regions): not taken for components, which have exactly one placement, so a property says the same thing with less text and stays readable by integrity rules as c.placement. The binding of records to a class is a relation, kept as the tenant class's binds list.

Tenant classes by flag, by plan or by both: a class takes at most one selector (tenant-class.selector) so its membership is one condition; Harbour tenants are the tenants with the regulated-sector flag on.

Checking per scenario (a scenario names a tenant's region and a machine moves its data): not taken for placement. The structure decides residency for every tenant of the class whichever region it was provisioned in, with no inputs to choose; a scenario would check only the regions it happened to name. The run-time part, an exception expiring and its copies being purged, stays an obligation shown by evidence.

Exceptions that expire by a date written in the specification: not taken. A specification states classes of exception, not approvals; maxDuration, renewalWindow and purgeWithin record the bounds of one approval, and status records that a class of exception is no longer in force (expired or revoked covers nothing).

The purge after expiry as a freshness or erasure bound of the excepted copy: not taken, because it weakens the copy's own bounds for every tenant (the fold's mistake); purgeWithin belongs to the exception.
data.consequences: Harbourline BR-04 and BR-05 are written with no scenario (tests/fixtures/residency/harbourline.jsonc). Placement is static: a component placed per-region is trusted to route each tenant to its home instance, which only evidence about the running system shows. The exception lifecycle (expiry, renewal within the window, purge within the bound) is recorded, not executed. Fields are not regions: a copy of a bound record is bound whatever fields it holds, and a reference-only payload is stated by an integrity rule over the copy's fields.
data.context: A fold of 26 business requirements for a multi-tenant platform (Harbourline BR-04, BR-05, BR-09, BR-18, BR-24) could not state residency against anything real: the format had no region, so every rule became a scenario boolean (a harbour flag in a step payload) or prose, and an exception edge copy was given a 72 hour freshness bound that weakened the existing 5 s purge of edge copies. Residency has to compose with records, copies, retention and erasure bounds and with the access model (flags, plans, roles), not duplicate them.
data.decision: Four additions. A region entity. A tenant class entity that selects tenants by one feature flag or one plan (or every tenant), names the regions its tenants may be provisioned in, a confinement (home, provisioned-regions or none) and the records it binds. Two component properties, placement (per-region, fixed or global) and regions, and one relationship property, carries (the records a data flow passes on). A residency exception entity naming one copy or flow of a tenant class, the feature, the approving role, maxDuration, renewalWindow, purgeWithin, the residual and a status. Validation (src/core/residency.js) follows each bound record to its owner, the holder of each copy and both ends of each carrying relationship, and reports residency.record-outside, residency.copy-outside or residency.flow-outside where the component cannot keep a tenant of the class in its permitted regions, unless an active exception names that copy or flow; plus residency.placement-missing, residency.region-uncovered, component.placement-regions, tenant-class.selector, tenant-class.provisioned-in and the exception rules (target, duration, purge, renewal). The properties are flat references, so integrity rules and recursive relations read them.
data.title: Residency: regions as entities, placement on components, confinement on tenant classes, checked on the structure

alternatives: Fold the pool into quota (a quota with scope pool): not taken. A quota is one counter per scope and window with one onExceed; a pool adds a group, fair shares, headroom, a multi-window rule, an exemption and a release, and keeping the per-tenant quota as each member's contribution keeps what one tenant is entitled to stated once.

Make capacity and fair share numbers of their own on the pool: not taken for rates, since the per-tenant quota already says what a tenant may use per window; perMember is kept for levels such as storage, which no quota counts.

Ask authors to write the pool's machine as an ordinary behavior: not taken. That is what the fold did; the rules then live in a hand-written machine that may differ from the pool it claims to model, with nothing to check them against.

Generate the machine into the specification as behavior entities (as cover-machines writes scenarios): not taken. The machine would be a second copy of the pool's meaning that drifts unless validation re-derives and compares it; deriving it when a scenario runs keeps one source.

Synthesise the machines as entities of the model at parse time: not taken. Entities have source positions and take part in rename and delete through the Lean model derivation; a derived machine has neither, and adding that machinery is larger than the need.

One machine per pool with per-member variables: not taken. The expression language has no conditional, so each window end would need a transition for every combination of member outcomes; one machine per member keeps each window end to one of a few guarded transitions, and the members read each other's usage for the pool total.

A scenario boolean saying a member is burst-eligible or throttled: not taken; eligibility is an event set by the reseller and the throttle follows from usage, so exploration over injected events covers the cases.
data.consequences: Harbourline BR-12 is written with no scenario boolean (tests/fixtures/pooled-quotas/harbourline.jsonc), and a claim that a burst-eligible client is never throttled after eligibility was set holds by exploration and fails when eligibility is effective only from the next window. A specification must say when a throttle lifts. The machines are not entities: renaming a pool does not rewrite claim expressions that name them, and the simulator panel and inspector do not show them (WG-5281). The model runs 1 to 4 members with equal contributions; unequal plans across members, usage that spans windows and revocation of eligibility are not modelled.
data.context: Harbourline BR-12 pools storage and automation-run quotas across a reseller's client tenants: a client may exceed its fair share while the pool has headroom, is throttled after three consecutive days over its share even with headroom unless burst-eligible, and burst eligibility is set by the reseller, applies from the day it is set and never to days already throttled. The format had per-tenant quotas only, so the fold became a hand-written machine with no pool, no headroom and a permanent throttle, and one of its invariants was false for burst-eligible clients but held because only one scenario was run. The rule must be checkable by exploration and compose with plans, quotas and the limit store.
data.decision: A quotaPool entity: memberClass and groupedBy (who shares), heldBy (the limit store), window and windowEnd (the day boundary event), limits (each a rate or a level whose per-member contribution is a per-tenant quota's limit or a perMember amount, with its usage event), overShare.consecutive, throttle (to fair-share or refuse, and a required release: a number of windows at or under the share, or never) and exemption (setBy role, capability, set event, effective same-window or next-window, retroactive). A member's fair share is its contribution and the capacity is the sum. The meaning is executable: src/core/pools.js derives one engine-input machine per limit and modelled member (<pool>-<limit>-m<k>, states normal and throttled, variables usage, day, overDays, underDays, throttledOn, burstSetOn, burstFrom, admitted, refused), and a scenario that lists the pool in pools runs them next to its behaviors, so simulate, the trace check and the Lean explorer decide claims over them. Validation checks the construct (pool.* codes) and claim expressions that read the machines.
data.title: Pooled quotas: a pool construct over per-tenant quotas whose meaning runs as derived machines
